Ko e meʻa ʻi he fai ʻe he tokolahi ke tohi fakaholo hono fakamatala ʻoe ngaahi meʻa ko ia ʻoku tui moʻoni ki ai ʻiate kitautolu,
Forasmuch as many have taken in hand to set forth in order a declaration of those things which are most surely believed among us,
‌ʻO hangē ko ia kuo tuku mai kiate kitautolu, ʻekinautolu naʻe mamata pau ki ai, pea hoko ko e kau faifekau ʻoe folofola, talu hono kamataʻanga;
Even as they delivered them unto us, which from the beginning were eyewitnesses, and ministers of the word;
‌ʻE Tiofilusi lelei, ko e meʻa ʻi heʻeku kumi fakatotolo ki he meʻa kotoa pē talu hano kamataʻanga, ʻoku ou loto ai ke u tohi fakaholo atu ia kiate koe,
It seemed good to me also, having had perfect understanding of all things from the very first, to write unto thee in order, most excellent Theophilus,
Koeʻuhi ke ke ʻilo hono moʻoni ʻoe ngaahi meʻa ko ia, ʻaia kuo akonekina ai koe.
That thou mightest know the certainty of those things, wherein thou hast been instructed.

NAʻE ai ʻi he ngaahi ʻaho ʻo Helota, ko e tuʻi ʻo Siutea, ʻae taulaʻeiki ʻe taha, ʻi he lakanga ʻo ʻApia, ko Sakalaia hono hingoa: pea ko hono uaifi naʻe mei he ngaahi ʻofefine ʻo ʻElone, pea ko ʻIlisapeti hono hingoa.
There was in the days of Herod, the king of Judaea, a certain priest named Zacharias, of the course of Abia: and his wife was of the daughters of Aaron, and her name was Elisabeth.
Pea naʻa na angatonu fakatouʻosi pe he ʻao ʻoe ʻOtua, ʻo na ʻalu taʻehala ʻi he ngaahi fekau mo e tuʻutuʻuni kotoa pē ʻae ʻEiki.
And they were both righteous before God, walking in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord blameless.
Pea naʻe ʻikai haʻana tama, koeʻuhi naʻe paʻa ʻa ʻIlisapeti, pea kuo na motuʻa fakatouʻosi pe.
And they had no child, because that Elisabeth was barren, and they both were now well stricken in years.
Pea pehē, ʻi heʻene fai ki he ngāue fakataulaʻeiki, ʻi he ʻao ʻoe ʻOtua, ʻi he lakanga ʻo hono vahe,
And it came to pass, that while he executed the priest’s office before God in the order of his course,
Ko hono lakanga, ʻo hangē ko hono anga ʻoe ngāue fakataulaʻeiki, ke tutu ʻae meʻa namu lelei ʻi heʻene hū ki he potu tapu ʻae ʻEiki.
According to the custom of the priest’s office, his lot was to burn incense when he went into the temple of the Lord.
Pea naʻe lotu ʻae fuʻu kakai kotoa pē ʻituʻa, ʻi he lolotonga ʻae tutu ʻoe ʻakau namu lelei.
And the whole multitude of the people were praying without at the time of incense.
Pea naʻe hā mai kiate ia ha ʻāngelo ʻae ʻEiki, ʻoku tuʻu ia ʻi he potu fakatoʻomataʻu ʻoe ʻesifeilaulau ʻoe ʻakau namu lelei.
And there appeared unto him an angel of the Lord standing on the right side of the altar of incense.
Pea tāfuʻua ʻa Sakalaia ʻi heʻene mamata ki ai, pea tō kiate ia ʻae manavahē.
And when Zacharias saw him, he was troubled, and fear fell upon him.
Ka naʻe pehē ʻe he ʻāngelo kiate ia, “Sakalaia, ʻoua te ke manavahē, he kuo tau hoʻo lotu; pea ʻe fāʻeleʻi ʻe ho uaifi ko ʻIlisapeti, ʻae tama kiate koe, pea te ke ui hono hingoa ko Sione.
But the angel said unto him, Fear not, Zacharias: for thy prayer is heard; and thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son, and thou shalt call his name John.
Pea te ke maʻu ai ʻae fiefia mo e nekeneka; pea ʻe fiefia ʻae tokolahi ʻi heʻene fanauʻi.
And thou shalt have joy and gladness; and many shall rejoice at his birth.
Koeʻuhi ʻe lahi ia ʻi he ʻao ʻoe ʻEiki, pea ʻe ʻikai te ne inu ʻae uaine pe ha inu fakakona; pea ʻe fonu ia ʻi he Laumālie Māʻoniʻoni, ʻio, mei he manāva ʻo ʻene faʻē.
For he shall be great in the sight of the Lord, and shall drink neither wine nor strong drink; and he shall be filled with the Holy Ghost, even from his mother’s womb.
Pea ʻe fakatafoki ʻe ia ʻae tokolahi ʻoe fānau ʻa ʻIsileli ki he ʻEiki ko honau ʻOtua.
And many of the children of Israel shall he turn to the Lord their God.
Pea ʻe muʻomuʻa ia ʻiate ia ʻi he anga mo e mālohi ʻo ʻIlaisiā, ‘Ke fakatafoki ʻae loto ʻoe mātuʻa ki he fānau,’ mo e talangataʻa ki he poto ʻoe angatonu; ke teuʻi ʻae kakai ke lelei maʻae ʻEiki.”

And he shall go before him in the spirit and power of Elias, to turn the hearts of the fathers to the children, and the disobedient to the wisdom of the just; to make ready a people prepared for the Lord.
Pea pehē ʻe Sakalaia ki he ʻāngelo, “Te u ʻilo ʻi he hā ʻae meʻa ni? He ko e tangata motuʻa au, pea kuo lahi ʻae taʻu ʻo hoku uaifi.”
And Zacharias said unto the angel, Whereby shall I know this? for I am an old man, and my wife well stricken in years.
Pea lea ʻae ʻāngelo, ʻo pehēange kiate ia, “Ko au Kepaleli, ʻoku ou tuʻu ʻi he ʻao ʻoe ʻOtua; pea kuo fekau au ke u lea kiate koe, mo fakahā kiate koe ʻae ngaahi meʻa fakafiefia ni.
And the angel answering said unto him, I am Gabriel, that stand in the presence of God; and am sent to speak unto thee, and to shew thee these glad tidings.
Pea vakai, te ke noa koe, ʻe ʻikai te ke faʻa lea, ʻo aʻu ki he ʻaho ʻe hoko ai ʻae ngaahi meʻa ni, ko e meʻa ʻi hoʻo taʻetui ki heʻeku ngaahi lea, ʻaia ʻe fakamoʻoni ʻi hono kuonga.”
And, behold, thou shalt be dumb, and not able to speak, until the day that these things shall be performed, because thou believest not my words, which shall be fulfilled in their season.
Pea naʻe tatali ʻae kakai kia Sakalaia, pea naʻa nau ofo ʻi heʻene tuai mai mei he potu tapu.
And the people waited for Zacharias, and marvelled that he tarried so long in the temple.
Pea kuo haʻu ia kituʻa, pea ʻikai te ne faʻa lea kiate kinautolu: pea nau ʻilo ai kuo hā mai ha meʻa kiate ia ʻi he potu tapu: he naʻe kamokamo ia kiate kinautolu, pea taʻelea.
And when he came out, he could not speak unto them: and they perceived that he had seen a vision in the temple: for he beckoned unto them, and remained speechless.
Pea pehē, ʻi he toki hili ʻae ngaahi ʻaho ʻo ʻene ngāue, naʻe ʻalu ia ki hono fale.
And it came to pass, that, as soon as the days of his ministration were accomplished, he departed to his own house.
Pea hili ʻae ngaahi ʻaho ko ia, naʻe tuituʻia ʻa hono uaifi ko ʻIlisapeti, pea naʻe nofo ia ʻi he lilo, ʻi he māhina ʻe nima, ʻo ne pehē,
And after those days his wife Elisabeth conceived, and hid herself five months, saying,
“Kuo fai pehē ʻe he ʻEiki kiate au, ʻi he ngaahi ʻaho naʻa ne vakaiʻi au, ke toʻo ʻiate au hoku manukiʻanga ʻi he kakai.”
Thus hath the Lord dealt with me in the days wherein he looked on me, to take away my reproach among men.
Pea ʻi hono ono ʻoe māhina, naʻe fekau ʻe he ʻOtua ʻae ʻāngelo ko Kepaleli ki he kolo ʻe taha ʻi Kāleli, ko Nāsaleti hono hingoa,
And in the sixth month the angel Gabriel was sent from God unto a city of Galilee, named Nazareth,
ki ha tāupoʻou ʻi he fale ʻo Tevita, kuo fakanofo ki he tangata naʻe hingoa ko Siosefa; pea ko e hingoa ʻoe tāupoʻou ko Mele.
To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David; and the virgin’s name was Mary.
Pea haʻu ʻae ʻāngelo kiate ia, ʻo ne pehē, “Siʻotoʻofa, ʻoku ke ʻofeina lahi, ʻoku ʻiate koe ʻae ʻEiki: ʻoku ke monūʻia ʻi he fefine fulipē.”
And the angel came in unto her, and said, Hail, thou that art highly favoured, the Lord is with thee: blessed art thou among women.
Pea kuo mamata ia ki ai, pea tāfuʻua ia ʻi heʻene lea, mo ne fifili ʻi hono loto, pe ko e hā hono ʻuhinga ʻoe fetapa ko ia.
And when she saw him, she was troubled at his saying, and cast in her mind what manner of salutation this should be.
Pea pehē ʻe he ʻāngelo kiate ia, “Mele, ʻoua ʻe manavahē: he ʻoku ke ʻofeina mei he ʻOtua.
And the angel said unto her, Fear not, Mary: for thou hast found favour with God.
Pea vakai, te ke tuituʻia ʻi ho manāva, pea fāʻeleʻi ʻae tama, pea ke ui hono huafa ko Sisu.
And, behold, thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and bring forth a son, and shalt call his name JESUS.
Pea ʻe lahi ia, pea ʻe ui ia ko e ʻAlo ʻoe Fungani Māʻolunga; ʻe ange kiate ia ʻe he ʻEiki ko e ʻOtua ʻae nofoʻa ʻo ʻene tamai ko Tevita:
He shall be great, and shall be called the Son of the Highest: and the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David:
Pea ʻe pule ia ki he fale ʻo Sēkope ʻo taʻengata; pea ʻe ʻikai hano ngataʻanga ʻo ʻene pule.”
And he shall reign over the house of Jacob for ever; and of his kingdom there shall be no end.
Pea pehē ʻe Mele ki he ʻāngelo, “ʻE fēfē ai ʻae meʻa ni, heʻeku ʻikai te u ʻiloa ha tangata?”
Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?

Pea lea ʻae ʻāngelo, ʻo pehēange kiate ia, “ʻE hoko mai ʻae Laumālie Māʻoniʻoni kiate koe, pea ʻe fakamalū koe ʻe he mālohi ʻoe Fungani Māʻolunga; pea ko ia foki ʻe ui ai ʻae hako māʻoniʻoni te ke fāʻeleʻi ko e ʻAlo ʻoe ʻOtua.

And the angel answered and said unto her, The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God.
Pea vakai, ko ho kāinga ko ʻIlisapeti, kuo tuituʻia ia ʻi he tama ʻi heʻene motuʻa: pea ko hono ono mahina eni ʻo ia naʻe ui koe paʻa.
And, behold, thy cousin Elisabeth, she hath also conceived a son in her old age: and this is the sixth month with her, who was called barren.
He ʻoku ʻikai ha meʻa ʻe faingataʻa ki he ʻOtua.”
For with God nothing shall be impossible.
Pea pehē ʻe Mele, “Vakai, ko e kaunanga au ʻae ʻEiki; ke hoko mai kiate au ʻo hangē ko hoʻo lea. Pea naʻe ʻalu ʻae ʻāngelo ʻiate ia.”
And Mary said, Behold the handmaid of the Lord; be it unto me according to thy word. And the angel departed from her.
Pea tuʻu hake ʻa Mele, ʻi he ngaahi ʻaho ko ia, ʻo ʻalu fakavave ki he fonua moʻunga, ki ha kolo ʻo Siuta;
And Mary arose in those days, and went into the hill country with haste, into a city of Juda;
Pea naʻe hū ia ki he fale ʻo Sakalaia, ʻo fetapa kia ʻIlisapeti.
And entered into the house of Zacharias, and saluted Elisabeth.
Pea naʻe pehē, kuo fanongo ʻa ʻIlisapeti ki he fetapa ʻa Mele, pea hopohopo ʻae tama ʻi hono manāva; pea fakafonu ʻa ʻIlisapeti ʻi he Laumālie Māʻoniʻoni:
And it came to pass, that, when Elisabeth heard the salutation of Mary, the babe leaped in her womb; and Elisabeth was filled with the Holy Ghost:
Pea naʻe lea ʻaki ʻe ia ʻae leʻo lahi, ʻo ne pehē, “ʻOku ke monūʻia koe ʻi he fefine kotoa pē pea ʻoku monūʻia mo e fua ʻo ho manāva.
And she spake out with a loud voice, and said, Blessed art thou among women, and blessed is the fruit of thy womb.
Pea ʻoku fēfē nai eni kiate au, koeʻuhi kuo haʻu ʻae faʻē ʻa hoku ʻEiki kiate au?
And whence is this to me, that the mother of my Lord should come to me?
Pea vakai, kuo ongo leva ʻae leʻo ʻa hoʻo fetapa ki hoku telinga, pea hopohopo fiefia ʻae tama ʻi hoku manāva.
For, lo, as soon as the voice of thy salutation sounded in mine ears, the babe leaped in my womb for joy.
Pea ʻoku monūʻia ʻaia kuo tui: koeʻuhi ʻe fakamoʻoni ʻae ngaahi meʻa ko ia ʻaia naʻe fakahā kiate ia mei he ʻEiki.”
And blessed is she that believed: for there shall be a performance of those things which were told her from the Lord.
Pea pehē ʻe Mele, “ʻOku fakahikihiki ʻae ʻEiki ʻe hoku laumālie,
And Mary said, My soul doth magnify the Lord,
Pea ʻoku fiefia hoku laumālie ʻi he ʻOtua ko hoku fakamoʻui.
And my spirit hath rejoiced in God my Saviour.
He kuo ne vakai ʻe ia ʻae vaivai ʻa ʻene kaunanga: Vakai, ngata mei he ʻaho ni ʻe ui au ko e monūʻia ʻe he ngaahi toʻutangata kotoa pē.
For he hath regarded the low estate of his handmaiden: for, behold, from henceforth all generations shall call me blessed.
He ko ia ʻoku māfimafi kuo ne fai kiate au ʻae ngaahi meʻa lahi; pea ʻoku māʻoniʻoni hono huafa.
For he that is mighty hath done to me great things; and holy is his name.
Pea ʻoku ʻiate kinautolu ʻoku manavahē kiate ia ʻa ʻene ʻaloʻofa Mei he toʻutangata ki he toʻutangata.
And his mercy is on them that fear him from generation to generation.
Kuo fakahā mai ʻe ia ʻae mālohi ʻo hono nima; Pea kuo veteki ʻe ia ʻae laukau ʻi he ngaoʻi ʻa honau loto.
He hath shewed strength with his arm; he hath scattered the proud in the imagination of their hearts.
Kuo fakahifo ʻe ia ʻae mālohi mei he ngaahi nofoʻanga, Pea kuo ne hakeakiʻi ʻakinautolu naʻe māʻulalo.
He hath put down the mighty from their seats, and exalted them of low degree.
Kuo fakamākona ʻe ia ʻae fiekaia, ʻaki ʻae ngaahi meʻa lelei; Ka ne tekeʻi atu ʻae maʻumeʻa ke masiva.
He hath filled the hungry with good things; and the rich he hath sent empty away.
Kuo tokoni ʻe ia ʻa ʻene tamaioʻeiki ko ʻIsileli, ʻI heʻene manatu ki he ʻaloʻofa;
He hath holpen his servant Israel, in remembrance of his mercy;
Kia ʻEpalahame, mo hono hako ʻo lauikuonga, ʻO hangē ko ʻene lea ki heʻetau ngaahi tamai.”
As he spake to our fathers, to Abraham, and to his seed for ever.
Pea naʻa na nonofo mo Mele ʻi he māhina nai ʻe tolu, pea toki ʻalu ia ki hono fale.
And Mary abode with her about three months, and returned to her own house.
Pea kuo hokosia ʻae ʻaho ke fāʻele ai ʻa ʻIlisapeti; pea fāʻeleʻi ʻe ia ʻae tama.
Now Elisabeth’s full time came that she should be delivered; and she brought forth a son.
Pea fanongo ʻa hono kaungāʻapi mo hono kāinga, kuo fakahā ʻe he ʻEiki ʻae ʻaloʻofa lahi kiate ia; pea nau fiefia mo ia.
And her neighbours and her cousins heard how the Lord had shewed great mercy upon her; and they rejoiced with her.
Pea pehē, ʻi hono ʻaho valu naʻa nau omi ke kamu ʻae tamasiʻi; pea naʻa nau ui ia ko Sakalaia, ʻo hangē ko e hingoa ʻo ʻene tamai.
And it came to pass, that on the eighth day they came to circumcise the child; and they called him Zacharias, after the name of his father.
Pea leaange ʻene faʻē, ʻo ne pehē, “ʻE ʻikai, kae ui ia ko Sione.”
And his mother answered and said, Not so; but he shall be called John.
Pea naʻa nau pehē kiate ia, “ʻOku ʻikai hao kāinga ʻoku ui ʻi he hingoa ko ia.”
And they said unto her, There is none of thy kindred that is called by this name.
Pea nau kamokamo ki heʻene tamai, pe ko e hā hono loto ke ui ia.
And they made signs to his father, how he would have him called.
Pea ne meʻa ke ʻomi ʻae tohiʻanga, pea tohi ʻe ia, ʻo pehē, “Ko Sione hono hingoa.” Pea naʻa nau ofo ai kotoa pē.
And he asked for a writing table, and wrote, saying, His name is John. And they marvelled all.
Pea matoʻo leva hono ngutu, pea mo hono ʻelelo, pea lea ia ʻo fakamālō ki he ʻOtua.
And his mouth was opened immediately, and his tongue loosed, and he spake, and praised God.
Pea naʻe tō ʻae manavahē ki he kakai kotoa pē naʻa nau nonofo ʻi he potu ko ia: pea naʻe ongoongoa ai ʻae ngaahi meʻa ni kotoa pē ʻi he fonua moʻunga kotoa pē ʻo Siutea.
And fear came on all that dwelt round about them: and all these sayings were noised abroad throughout all the hill country of Judaea.
Pea ko kinautolu kotoa pē naʻe fanongo ki ai, naʻa nau fifili ʻi honau loto, mo pehē, “ʻE fēfē nai ʻae anga ʻae tama ni!” Pea naʻe ʻiate ia ʻae nima ʻoe ʻEiki.
And all they that heard them laid them up in their hearts, saying, What manner of child shall this be! And the hand of the Lord was with him.
Pea naʻe fakafonu ʻa ʻene tamai ko Sakalaia ʻi he Laumālie Māʻoniʻoni, pea kikite ia, ʻo pehē,
And his father Zacharias was filled with the Holy Ghost, and prophesied, saying,
“Fakafetaʻi ki he ʻEiki ko e ʻOtua ʻo ʻIsileli; He kuo ne ʻaʻahi mo huhuʻi ʻa hono kakai,
Blessed be the Lord God of Israel; for he hath visited and redeemed his people,
Pea kuo ne fokotuʻu ʻe ia ʻae mālohi ʻoe fakamoʻui kiate kitautolu, ʻI he fale ʻo ʻene tamaioʻeiki ko Tevita;
And hath raised up an horn of salvation for us in the house of his servant David;
‌ʻO hangē ko ʻene folofola ʻi he ngutu ʻo ʻene kau palōfita māʻoniʻoni, Naʻe ai talu ʻae tupuʻanga ʻo māmani:
As he spake by the mouth of his holy prophets, which have been since the world began:
Koeʻuhi ke fakamoʻui ʻakitautolu mei hotau ngaahi fili, Mo e nima ʻokinautolu kotoa pē ʻoku fehiʻa kiate kitautolu;
That we should be saved from our enemies, and from the hand of all that hate us;
Ke fakamoʻoni ʻae ʻaloʻofa ki heʻetau mātuʻa, Mo manatu ki heʻene fuakava māʻoniʻoni;
To perform the mercy promised to our fathers, and to remember his holy covenant;
‌ʻAe fuakava ʻaia naʻa ne fuakava ʻaki ki heʻetau tamai ko ʻEpalahame,
The oath which he sware to our father Abraham,
Ke tuku ʻe ia kiate kitautolu, Ke tau hao mei he nima ʻo hotau ngaahi fili, Pea tau tauhi ia taʻemanavahē,
That he would grant unto us, that we being delivered out of the hand of our enemies might serve him without fear,
‌ʻI he māʻoniʻoni mo e angatonu ʻi hono ʻao, ʻi he ʻaho kotoa pē ʻo ʻetau moʻui.
In holiness and righteousness before him, all the days of our life.
Pea ko koe, ʻe tama, ʻe ui koe ko e palōfita ʻoe Fungani Māʻolunga: He te ke muʻomuʻa ʻi he ʻao ʻoe ʻEiki ke teuteu hono hala;
And thou, child, shalt be called the prophet of the Highest: for thou shalt go before the face of the Lord to prepare his ways;
Ke fakaʻilo ʻae fakamoʻui ki hono kakai ʻi he fakamolemole ʻo ʻenau hia,
To give knowledge of salvation unto his people by the remission of their sins,
Ko e meʻa ʻi he ʻaloʻofa ongongofua ʻa hotau ʻOtua; ʻAia kuo hoko mei ai ʻae hengihengi ʻoe ʻaho mei ʻolunga kiate kitautolu,
Through the tender mercy of our God; whereby the dayspring from on high hath visited us,
Ke fakamaama kiate kinautolu ʻoku nofo ʻi he fakapoʻuli mo e ʻata ʻoe mate, Ke fakahinohino hotau vaʻe ki he hala ʻoe fiemālie.”
To give light to them that sit in darkness and in the shadow of death, to guide our feet into the way of peace.
Pea naʻe tupu ʻae tama, pea fakaʻaʻau ʻo mālohi ʻi he laumālie, pea naʻa ne ʻi he toafa ʻo aʻu ki he ʻaho naʻa ne fakahā ai ia ki ʻIsileli.
And the child grew, and waxed strong in spirit, and was in the deserts till the day of his shewing unto Israel.
Pea pehē, naʻe fai ʻae fono ʻe Sisa ʻAokositusi, ʻi he ngaahi ʻaho ko ia, ke tohi ʻae kakai kotoa pē ʻoe puleʻanga.
And it came to pass in those days, that there went out a decree from Caesar Augustus, that all the world should be taxed.
(Pea naʻe fuofua fai ʻae tohi ni ʻi he pule ʻa Kilinio ʻi Silia.)
(And this taxing was first made when Cyrenius was governor of Syria.)
Pea naʻe taki taha ʻalu ʻae kakai kotoa pē ki hono potu, ke tohi ai ia.
And all went to be taxed, every one into his own city.
Pea ʻalu hake foki ʻa Siosefa mei Kāleli, mei he kolo ko Nāsaleti, ki Siutea, ki he Kolo ʻo Tevita, ʻoku ui ko Petelihema; (he naʻa ne ʻoe fale mo e faʻahinga ʻo Tevita;)
And Joseph also went up from Galilee, out of the city of Nazareth, into Judaea, unto the city of David, which is called Bethlehem; (because he was of the house and lineage of David:)
Ke tohi ia mo hono uaifi ko Mele, naʻe fakanofo, kuo feitama ia.
To be taxed with Mary his espoused wife, being great with child.
Pea naʻe lolotonga ʻena ʻi ai, pea pehē, kuo kakato hono ngaahi ʻaho ke fāʻele ai ia.
And so it was, that, while they were there, the days were accomplished that she should be delivered.
Pea fāʻeleʻi ʻe ia ʻae tama ko hono ʻolopoʻou, pea ne takatakai ʻaki ia ʻae kofu, ʻo fakatokoto ia ʻi he ʻaiʻanga kai ʻoe manu; koeʻuhi naʻe ʻikai te nau hao ʻi he fale talifononga.
And she brought forth her firstborn son, and wrapped him in swaddling clothes, and laid him in a manger; because there was no room for them in the inn.
Pea naʻe ʻi he fonua ko ia ʻae kau tauhi sipi ʻoku nofo ʻi he ngoue, ʻo leʻohi ʻenau fanga sipi ʻi he poʻuli.
And there were in the same country shepherds abiding in the field, keeping watch over their flock by night.
Pea ʻiloange, naʻe tuʻu mai kiate kinautolu ʻae ʻāngelo ʻae ʻEiki, pea malama ʻae nāunau ʻoe ʻEiki ʻo takatakai ʻakinautolu: pea naʻa nau manavahē ʻaupito.
And, lo, the angel of the Lord came upon them, and the glory of the Lord shone round about them: and they were sore afraid.
Pea pehē ʻe he ʻāngelo kiate kinautolu, “ʻOua ʻe manavahē: vakai, he ʻoku ou ʻomi kiate kimoutolu ʻae ongoongolelei ʻoe fiefia lahi, ʻaia ʻe hoko ki he kakai fulipē.
And the angel said unto them, Fear not: for, behold, I bring you good tidings of great joy, which shall be to all people.
He kuo ʻaloʻi kiate kimoutolu ʻi he ʻaho ni, ʻi he Kolo ʻo Tevita, ʻae Fakamoʻui, ʻaia ko Kalaisi ko e ʻEiki.
For unto you is born this day in the city of David a Saviour, which is Christ the Lord.
Pea ko e fakaʻilonga eni kiate kimoutolu; te mou ʻilo ʻae tamasiʻi kuo takatakai ʻaki ia ʻae kofu, pea tokoto ia ʻi he ʻaiʻanga kai ʻoe manu.”
And this shall be a sign unto you; Ye shall find the babe wrapped in swaddling clothes, lying in a manger.
Pea fakafokifā pe kuo ʻi he ʻāngelo ʻae tokolahi ʻoe kau ʻāngelo mei he langi, ʻonau fakamālō ki he ʻOtua, ʻo pehē,
And suddenly there was with the angel a multitude of the heavenly host praising God, and saying,
“Fakafetaʻi ki he ʻOtua ʻi ʻolunga, Pea ʻi māmani ʻae melino, ko e ʻofa ki he kakai.”
Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, good will toward men.

Pea pehē, ʻi he liliu ange ʻae kau ʻāngelo ki he langi meiate kinautolu, naʻe fepehēʻaki ʻe he kau tauhi sipi, “Ke tau ō eni ki Petelihema, ʻo mamata ki he meʻa ni kuo fai, ʻaia kuo fakahā mai ʻe he ʻEiki kiate kitautolu.”

And it came to pass, as the angels were gone away from them into heaven, the shepherds said one to another, Let us now go even unto Bethlehem, and see this thing which is come to pass, which the Lord hath made known unto us.
Pea naʻa nau omi fakavave, ʻo ʻilo ʻa Mele, mo Siosefa, mo e tama ʻoku tokoto ʻi he ʻaiʻanga kai ʻoe manu.
And they came with haste, and found Mary, and Joseph, and the babe lying in a manger.
Pea kuo nau mamata, pea nau ongoongoa ʻae lea naʻe fakahā kiate kinautolu ʻi he tama ni.
And when they had seen it, they made known abroad the saying which was told them concerning this child.
Pea ofo ai ʻakinautolu kotoa pē naʻe fanongo ʻi he ngaahi meʻa ko ia naʻe fakahā ʻe he kau tauhi sipi kiate kinautolu.
And all they that heard it wondered at those things which were told them by the shepherds.
Ka naʻe faʻoa ʻe Mele ʻae ngaahi meʻa ni kotoa pē ki hono loto, ʻo fifili ki ai.
But Mary kept all these things, and pondered them in her heart.
Pea naʻe liu mai ʻae kau tauhi sipi, ʻo fakamālō mo fakafetaʻi ki he ʻOtua, koeʻuhi ko e ngaahi meʻa kotoa pē kuo nau fanongo mo mamata ai, ʻo hangē ko ia ne fakahā kiate kinautolu.
And the shepherds returned, glorifying and praising God for all the things that they had heard and seen, as it was told unto them.
Pea ʻi heʻene kakato ʻae ʻaho ʻe valu naʻe kamu ʻae tama, pea ui hono huafa ko Sisu, ʻaia naʻe fakahingoa ʻe he ʻāngelo kae teʻeki tuituʻia ia ʻi he manāva.
And when eight days were accomplished for the circumcising of the child, his name was called JESUS, which was so named of the angel before he was conceived in the womb.
Pea kuo hili ʻae ngaahi ʻaho ʻo ʻena fakamaʻa, ʻo fakatatau ki he fono ʻa Mōsese, naʻa nau ʻomi ia ki Selūsalema ke ʻatu ia ki he ʻEiki;
And when the days of her purification according to the law of Moses were accomplished, they brought him to Jerusalem, to present him to the Lord;
(ʻO hangē ko ia kuo tohi ʻi he fono ʻae ʻEiki, “Ko e tama kotoa pe, ʻae ʻolopoʻou, ʻe ui ia ko e tapu ki he ʻEiki;”)
(As it is written in the law of the LORD, Every male that openeth the womb shall be called holy to the Lord;)
Pea ke ʻatu ʻae feilaulau, ʻo fakatatau mo ia ʻoku fakahā mai ʻi he fono ʻae ʻEiki, “Ko e ongo kulukulu, pe ko e lupe mui ʻe ua.”
And to offer a sacrifice according to that which is said in the law of the Lord, A pair of turtledoves, or two young pigeons.

Pea vakai, naʻe ʻi Selūsalema ʻae tangata, ko Simione hono hingoa; pea naʻe angatonu ʻae tangata ko ia mo faʻa lotu, mo tatali ki he fiemālieʻanga ʻo ʻIsileli: pea naʻe ʻiate ia ʻae Laumālie Māʻoniʻoni.
And, behold, there was a man in Jerusalem, whose name was Simeon; and the same man was just and devout, waiting for the consolation of Israel: and the Holy Ghost was upon him.
Pea naʻe fakahā mai kiate ia ʻe he Laumālie Māʻoniʻoni, ʻe ʻikai mate ia, kaeʻoua ke ne mamata ki he Kalaisi ʻae ʻEiki.
And it was revealed unto him by the Holy Ghost, that he should not see death, before he had seen the Lord’s Christ.
Pea haʻu ia ʻi he Laumālie ki he falelotu tatau ki hono anga ʻoe fono,
And he came by the Spirit into the temple: and when the parents brought in the child Jesus, to do for him after the custom of the law,
Naʻa ne toki toʻo hake ia ʻi hono nima, pea fakafetaʻi ki he ʻOtua, ʻo ne pehē,
Then took he him up in his arms, and blessed God, and said,
“ʻE ʻEiki, ko eni, ʻoku ke tukuange ʻa hoʻo tamaioʻeiki ke fononga ʻi he fiemālie, ʻO hangē ko hoʻo folofola:
Lord, now lettest thou thy servant depart in peace, according to thy word:
He kuo mamata ʻa hoku mata ki hoʻo fakamoʻui,
For mine eyes have seen thy salvation,
‌ʻAia kuo ke teuteu ʻi he ʻao ʻoe kakai kotoa pē;
Which thou hast prepared before the face of all people;
Ko e maama ke fakamaamaʻaki ʻae Senitaile, Mo e nāunau ʻo hoʻo kakai ko ʻIsileli.”
A light to lighten the Gentiles, and the glory of thy people Israel.
Pea ofo ʻa Siosefa mo ʻene faʻē ʻi he ngaahi meʻa ko ia naʻe fakahā ʻiate ia.
And Joseph and his mother marvelled at those things which were spoken of him.

Pea tāpuakiʻi ʻe Simione ʻakinaua, ʻo ne pehē ki heʻene faʻē ko Mele, “Vakai, kuo fokotuʻu ʻae tamasiʻi ni ko e tūkiaʻanga mo e toetuʻuʻanga ʻoe tokolahi ʻi ʻIsileli pea ko e fakaʻilonga ke lea kovi ki ai;
And Simeon blessed them, and said unto Mary his mother, Behold, this child is set for the fall and rising again of many in Israel; and for a sign which shall be spoken against;
koeʻuhi ke hā ai ʻae ngaahi mahalo ʻoe loto ʻoe tokolahi: (ʻio, ʻe tui pea ʻasi ʻae heletā ʻi ho laumālie foki.”)
(Yea, a sword shall pierce through thy own soul also,) that the thoughts of many hearts may be revealed.
Pea naʻe ʻi ai ʻae fefine palōfita ko ʻAna, ko e ʻofefine ʻo Fanueli, ʻi he faʻahinga ʻo ʻAsa: naʻe lahi hono motuʻa, pea naʻa na nonofo mo hono husepāniti ʻi he taʻu ʻe fitu talu ʻene tāupoʻou;
And there was one Anna, a prophetess, the daughter of Phanuel, of the tribe of Aser: she was of a great age, and had lived with an husband seven years from her virginity;

ka ka nofo ai pe ia ko e fefine ia kuo mate hono husepāniti, pea kuo valungofulu ma fā ʻae taʻu ʻo ʻene motuʻa, pea ne ʻikai mahuʻi ia mei he falelotu lahi, ka naʻa ne ngāue ʻi he ʻaukai mo e faʻa lotu he pō mo e ʻaho.
And she was a widow of about fourscore and four years, which departed not from the temple, but served God with fastings and prayers night and day.
Pea ʻi heʻene haʻu ʻo feʻunga mo ia, naʻa ne ʻatu foki ʻae fakafetaʻi ki he ʻEiki, ʻo ne fakahā ia kiate kinautolu kotoa pē naʻe tatali ki he huhuʻi ʻi Selūsalema.
And she coming in that instant gave thanks likewise unto the Lord, and spake of him to all them that looked for redemption in Jerusalem.
Pea hili ʻena fai ʻae ngaahi meʻa kotoa pē, ʻo fakatatau ki he fono ʻae ʻEiki, naʻa nau foki mai ki Kāleli, ki hona kolo ko Nāsaleti.
And when they had performed all things according to the law of the Lord, they returned into Galilee, to their own city Nazareth.
Pea tupu ʻae tamasiʻi, pea mālohi ʻi he laumālie, pea fonu ia ʻi he poto: pea naʻe ʻiate ia ʻae ʻofa ʻae ʻOtua.
And the child grew, and waxed strong in spirit, filled with wisdom: and the grace of God was upon him.
Pea naʻe ʻalu ʻene mātuʻa ʻi he taʻu kotoa pē ki Selūsalema, ki he kātoanga ʻoe Lakaatu.
Now his parents went to Jerusalem every year at the feast of the passover.
Pea kuo hongofulu ma ua hono taʻu, pea nau ō hake ki Selūsalema, ʻo hangē ko hono anga ʻoe kātoanga.
And when he was twelve years old, they went up to Jerusalem after the custom of the feast.
Pea kuo nau fakaʻosi ʻae ngaahi ʻaho, ka ʻi heʻenau liliu mai, naʻe nofo pe ʻae tama ko Sisu ʻi Selūsalema: pea naʻe ʻikai ʻilo ʻe Siosefa mo ʻene faʻē.
And when they had fulfilled the days, as they returned, the child Jesus tarried behind in Jerusalem; and Joseph and his mother knew not of it.
Ka naʻe mahalo ʻakinaua ʻoku ʻi he fononga ia, pea fononga ʻi he ʻaho ʻe taha; pea toki kumi ia ʻi hona kāinga mo e kau fononga.
But they, supposing him to have been in the company, went a day’s journey; and they sought him among their kinsfolk and acquaintance.
Pea ʻi he ʻikai te na ʻilo ia, naʻa na foki atu ki Selūsalema, ko hono kumi.
And when they found him not, they turned back again to Jerusalem, seeking him.
Pea pehē, kuo hili ʻae ʻaho ʻe tolu, pea na toki ʻilo ia ʻi he falelotu lahi, ʻoku nofo ʻi he haʻohaʻonga ʻoe kau akonaki, ʻo fakafanongo kiate kinautolu, mo fakafehuʻi kiate kinautolu.
And it came to pass, that after three days they found him in the temple, sitting in the midst of the doctors, both hearing them, and asking them questions.
Pea ko kinautolu kotoa pē naʻe fanongo kiate ia, naʻa nau ofo ʻi heʻene poto mo ʻene tali ʻae fehuʻi.
And all that heard him were astonished at his understanding and answers.
Pea ʻi heʻena mamata kiate ia, ne na ofo ai ʻaupito: pea pehē ʻe heʻene faʻē kiate ia, “Tama, ko e hā kuo ke fai pehē ai kiate kimaua? Vakai, ko hoʻo tamai mo au kuo ma kumi koe ʻi he mamahi.”
And when they saw him, they were amazed: and his mother said unto him, Son, why hast thou thus dealt with us? behold, thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing.
Pea pehē ʻe ia kiate kinaua, “Ko e hā ʻoku mo kumi ai au? ʻIkai te mo ʻilo ʻoku ʻaʻaku ke fai ʻae ngāue ʻa ʻeku Tamai?”
And he said unto them, How is it that ye sought me? wist ye not that I must be about my Father’s business?
Ka naʻe ʻikai te na ʻilo hono ʻuhinga ʻoe lea ne ne lea ʻaki kiate kinaua.
And they understood not the saying which he spake unto them.
Pea ʻalu hifo ia mo kinaua, ʻo hoko ki Nāsaleti, pea anganofo ia kiate kinaua: ka naʻe faʻo ʻe heʻene faʻē ʻae ngaahi lea ni kotoa pē ki hono loto.
And he went down with them, and came to Nazareth, and was subject unto them: but his mother kept all these sayings in her heart.
Pea tupulaki ʻae poto ʻia Sisu mo e lahi, pea naʻe ʻofeina ia ʻe he ʻOtua mo e tangata.
And Jesus increased in wisdom and stature, and in favour with God and man.

Pea ʻi hono hongofulu ma nima ʻoe taʻu ʻoe pule ʻa Taipiliusi Sisa, ko e ʻeiki pule ʻa Ponito Pailato ʻi Siutea, pea tuʻi ai ʻa Helota ʻi Kāleli, pea tuʻi ʻa hono tokoua ko Filipe ʻi ʻAitulia mo e feituʻu ʻo Tilakonite, pea tuʻi ʻa Lisaniasi ʻi ʻApiline,

Now in the fifteenth year of the reign of Tiberius Caesar, Pontius Pilate being governor of Judaea, and Herod being tetrarch of Galilee, and his brother Philip tetrarch of Ituraea and of the region of Trachonitis, and Lysanias the tetrarch of Abilene,
Pea ko ʻAnasi mo Kaiafasi ko e ongo taulaʻeiki lahi ʻakinaua, naʻe hoko ʻae folofola ʻae ʻOtua kia Sione ko e foha ʻo Sakalaia ʻi he toafa.
Annas and Caiaphas being the high priests, the word of God came unto John the son of Zacharias in the wilderness.
Pea haʻu ia ki he potu fonua kotoa pē ʻo ofi ki Sioatani, ʻo ne malangaʻaki ʻae papitaiso ʻoe fakatomala ki he fakamolemole ʻoe angahala:
And he came into all the country about Jordan, preaching the baptism of repentance for the remission of sins;
‌ʻO hangē ko ia kuo tohi ʻi he tohi ʻae ngaahi lea ʻae palōfita ko ʻIsaia, ʻo pehē, “Ko e leʻo ʻoe tokotaha ʻoku kalanga ʻi he toafa, ‘Mou teuteu ʻae hala ʻo Sihova, pea fakatonutonu hono ʻaluʻanga.
As it is written in the book of the words of Esaias the prophet, saying, The voice of one crying in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of the Lord, make his paths straight.
‌ʻE tanu ʻae luo kotoa pē, ʻE holoki hifo ʻae moʻunga mo e tafungofunga kotoa pē; Pea ʻe fakatotonu ʻae pikopiko, Pea ʻe fakatokalelei ʻae ngaahi hala ʻoku tokatāmaki;
Every valley shall be filled, and every mountain and hill shall be brought low; and the crooked shall be made straight, and the rough ways shall be made smooth;
Pea ʻe mamata ʻae kakai kotoa pē ki he fakamoʻui ʻae ʻOtua.’”
And all flesh shall see the salvation of God.
Pea toki pehē ʻe ia ki he kakai kuo ʻalu ange ke nau papitaiso ʻiate ia, “ʻAe fānau ʻae ngata fekai, Ko hai ne ne valoki ʻakimoutolu ke mou puna mei he houhau ʻe haʻu?
Then said he to the multitude that came forth to be baptized of him, O generation of vipers, who hath warned you to flee from the wrath to come?

Ko ia mou fakahā ʻae ngaahi fua ʻoku ngali mo e fakatomala, pea ʻoua naʻa lau leva ʻi homou loto, ‘ʻOku mau tamai ʻaki ʻa ʻEpalahame:’ he ʻoku ou tala atu kiate kimoutolu, ʻOku faʻa fai ʻe he ʻOtua ke fakatupu ʻi he ngaahi maka ni ʻae fānau kia ʻEpalahame.

Bring forth therefore fruits worthy of repentance, and begin not to say within yourselves, We have Abraham to our father: for I say unto you, That God is able of these stones to raise up children unto Abraham.
Pea ko eni foki, kuo tuku ʻae toki ki he tefito ʻoe ngaahi ʻakau: pea ko ia, ka ʻilonga ʻae ʻakau ʻoku ʻikai tupu ai ʻae fua lelei ʻe tā hifo ia, ʻo laku ki he afi.”
And now also the axe is laid unto the root of the trees: every tree therefore which bringeth not forth good fruit is hewn down, and cast into the fire.
Pea fehuʻi ʻae kakai kiate ia, ʻo pehē, “Ko e hā nai te mau fai?”
And the people asked him, saying, What shall we do then?
Pea lea ia, ʻo pehēange kiate kinautolu, “Ko ia ʻoku maʻu ʻae kofutuʻa ʻe ua, ke ne foaki kiate ia ʻoku ʻikai maʻu; pea ko ia ʻoku maʻu ʻae meʻa kai, ke fai pehē foki.”
He answereth and saith unto them, He that hath two coats, let him impart to him that hath none; and he that hath meat, let him do likewise.
Pea haʻu foki ʻae kau tānaki tukuhau ke papitaiso, ʻonau pehē kiate ia, “ʻEiki, ko e hā te mau fai?”
Then came also publicans to be baptized, and said unto him, Master, what shall we do?
Pea pehē ʻe ia kiate kinautolu, “ʻOua naʻa mou maʻu ʻo lahi ʻi he meʻa kuo tuʻutuʻuni maʻamoutolu.”
And he said unto them, Exact no more than that which is appointed you.

Pea fehuʻi foki ʻe he kau tau kiate ia, ʻo pehē; “Pea ko e hā te mau fai?” Pea pehē ʻe ia kiate kinautolu, “ʻOua naʻa fai fakamālohi ki ha taha, pea ʻoua naʻa lohiakiʻi; pea mou fiemālie ʻi hoʻomou totongi.”
And the soldiers likewise demanded of him, saying, And what shall we do? And he said unto them, Do violence to no man, neither accuse any falsely; and be content with your wages.
Pea naʻe lolotonga ʻae ʻamanaki ʻae kakai, mo nau fifili kotoa pē ʻi honau loto kia Sione, pe ko e Kalaisi ia pe ʻikai;
And as the people were in expectation, and all men mused in their hearts of John, whether he were the Christ, or not;

Pea lea ʻa Sione, ʻo ne pehēange kiate kinautolu kotoa pē, “Ko e moʻoni ʻoku ou papitaiso ʻaki ʻakimoutolu ʻae vai; ka ʻoku haʻu ʻae tokotaha ʻoku mālohi ʻiate au, pea ʻoku ʻikai taau mo au ke u vete ʻae nonoʻo ʻo hono topuvaʻe: pea ʻe papitaiso ʻaki ʻe ia ʻakimoutolu ʻae Laumālie Māʻoniʻoni mo e afi:

John answered, saying unto them all, I indeed baptize you with water; but one mightier than I cometh, the latchet of whose shoes I am not worthy to unloose: he shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost and with fire:
‌ʻOku ʻi hono nima ʻa hono fohe, pea te ne fakamaʻa ʻaupito hono hahaʻanga, pea ʻe ia ʻae kafukafu ʻaki ʻae afi taʻemate.”
Whose fan is in his hand, and he will throughly purge his floor, and will gather the wheat into his garner; but the chaff he will burn with fire unquenchable.
Pea lahi ʻae meʻa kehekehe naʻa ne malangaʻaki ʻi heʻene enginaki ki he kakai.
And many other things in his exhortation preached he unto the people.
Ka naʻe valoki ʻe ia ʻa Helota ko e tuʻi, koeʻuhi ko Helotiasi ko e uaifi ʻo hono tokoua ko Filipe, pea mo e kovi kotoa pē ne fai ʻe Helota.
But Herod the tetrarch, being reproved by him for Herodias his brother Philip’s wife, and for all the evils which Herod had done,
Pea ne fakalahi ʻaki ʻae meʻa ni kotoa pē, ʻa ʻene fakahū ʻa Sione ki he fale fakapōpula.
Added yet this above all, that he shut up John in prison.
Pea kuo papitaiso ʻae kakai kotoa pē, pea pehē, ne papitaiso foki mo Sisu, pea ʻi heʻene lotu, ne matoʻo ʻae langi,
Now when all the people were baptized, it came to pass, that Jesus also being baptized, and praying, the heaven was opened,
Pea maliu hifo ʻae Laumālie Māʻoniʻoni kiate ia ʻo hangē ko e sino ʻoe lupe, pea hoko mai mo e leʻo mei he langi, ʻo pehē, “Ko hoku ʻAlo ʻofaʻanga koe; ʻoku ou fiemālie lahi ʻiate koe.”
And the Holy Ghost descended in a bodily shape like a dove upon him, and a voice came from heaven, which said, Thou art my beloved Son; in thee I am well pleased.
Pea kuo tolungofulu nai ʻae taʻu ʻo Sisu, ʻaia (naʻe ui) ko e foha ʻo Siosefa, ʻaia ko e foha ʻo Helai,
And Jesus himself began to be about thirty years of age, being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph, which was the son of Heli,
Ko e foha ia ʻo Matati, ko e foha ia ʻo Livai, ko e foha ia ʻo Melikai, ko e foha ia ʻo Sana, ko e foha ia ʻo Siosefa,
Which was the son of Matthat, which was the son of Levi, which was the son of Melchi, which was the son of Janna, which was the son of Joseph,
Ko e foha ia ʻo Matatiasi, ko e foha ia ʻo Emosi, ko e foha ia ʻo Neumi, ko e foha ia ʻo Esilai, ko e foha ia ʻo Naki,
Which was the son of Mattathias, which was the son of Amos, which was the son of Naum, which was the son of Esli, which was the son of Nagge,
Ko e foha ia ʻo Mati, ko e foha ia ʻo Matatiasi, ko e foha ia ʻo Semiai, ko e foha ia ʻo Siosefa, ko e foha ia ʻo Siuta,
Which was the son of Maath, which was the son of Mattathias, which was the son of Semei, which was the son of Joseph, which was the son of Juda,
Ko e foha ia ʻo Soana, ko e foha ia ʻo Lisa, ko e foha ia ʻo Solopepeli, ko e foha ia ʻo Saletieli, ko e foha ia ʻo Nilai,
Which was the son of Joanna, which was the son of Rhesa, which was the son of Zorobabel, which was the son of Salathiel, which was the son of Neri,
Ko e foha ia ʻo Milikai, ko e foha ia ʻo ʻAtai, ko e foha ia ʻo Kosami, ko e foha ia ʻo Elimotami, ko e foha ia ʻo ʻEa,
Which was the son of Melchi, which was the son of Addi, which was the son of Cosam, which was the son of Elmodam, which was the son of Er,
Ko e foha ia ʻo Sose, ko e foha ia ʻo ʻEliesa, ko e foha ia ʻo Solimi, ko e foha ia ʻo Matati, ko e foha ia ʻo Livai,
Which was the son of Jose, which was the son of Eliezer, which was the son of Jorim, which was the son of Matthat, which was the son of Levi,
Ko e foha ia ʻo Simione, ko e foha ia ʻo Siuta, ko e foha ia ʻo Siosefa, ko e foha ia Sonani, ko e foha ia ʻo Iliakimi,
Which was the son of Simeon, which was the son of Juda, which was the son of Joseph, which was the son of Jonan, which was the son of Eliakim,
Ko e foha ia ʻo Melia, ko e foha ia ʻo Menani, ko e foha ia ʻo Matata, ko e foha ia ʻo Netani, ko e foha ia ʻo Tevita,
Which was the son of Melea, which was the son of Menan, which was the son of Mattatha, which was the son of Nathan, which was the son of David,
Ko e foha ia ʻo Sese, ko e foha ia ʻo ʻOpeti, ko e foha ia ʻo Poasi, ko e foha ia ʻo Salimoni, ko e foha ia ʻo Neasoni,
Which was the son of Jesse, which was the son of Obed, which was the son of Booz, which was the son of Salmon, which was the son of Naasson,
Ko e foha ia ʻo ʻAminitape, ko e foha ia ʻo ʻElami, ko e foha ia ʻo Esiloni, ko e foha ia ʻo Felesi, ko e foha ia ʻo Siuta,
Which was the son of Aminadab, which was the son of Aram, which was the son of Esrom, which was the son of Phares, which was the son of Juda,
Ko e foha ia ʻo Sēkope, ko e foha ia ʻo ʻAisake, ko e foha ia ʻo ʻEpalahame, ko e foha ia ʻo Tela, ko e foha ia ʻo Nekoa,
Which was the son of Jacob, which was the son of Isaac, which was the son of Abraham, which was the son of Thara, which was the son of Nachor,
Ko e foha ia ʻo Seluki, ko e foha ia ʻo Lekoa, ko e foha ia ʻo Feleki, ko e foha ia ʻo Hepa, ko e foha ia ʻo Sala,
Which was the son of Saruch, which was the son of Ragau, which was the son of Phalec, which was the son of Heber, which was the son of Sala,
Ko e foha ia ʻo Kēnani, ko e foha ia ʻo ʻAfakisati, ko e foha ia ʻo Semi, ko e foha ia ʻo Noa, ko e foha ia ʻo Lemeki,
Which was the son of Cainan, which was the son of Arphaxad, which was the son of Sem, which was the son of Noe, which was the son of Lamech,
Ko e foha ia ʻo Metusela, ko e foha ia ʻo ʻInoke, ko e foha ia ʻo Seleti, ko e foha ia ʻo Melilieli, ko e foha ia ʻo Kēnani,
Which was the son of Mathusala, which was the son of Enoch, which was the son of Jared, which was the son of Maleleel, which was the son of Cainan,
Ko e foha ia ʻo ʻInosi, ko e foha ia ʻo Seti, ko e foha ia ʻo ʻAtama, ko e foha ia ʻoe ʻOtua.
Which was the son of Enos, which was the son of Seth, which was the son of Adam, which was the son of God.
Naʻe liu mai ʻa Sisu mei Sioatani, kuo fonu ʻi he Laumālie Māʻoniʻoni, pea naʻe tataki ia ʻe he Laumālie ki he toafa.
And Jesus being full of the Holy Ghost returned from Jordan, and was led by the Spirit into the wilderness,
Pea ʻahiʻahiʻi ia ʻe he tēvolo ʻi he ʻaho ʻe fāngofulu. Pea ko e ngaahi ʻaho ko ia naʻe ʻikai te ne kai ai ha meʻa: pea hili ia, naʻa ne fiekaia.
Being forty days tempted of the devil. And in those days he did eat nothing: and when they were ended, he afterward hungered.
Pea pehē ʻe he tēvolo kiate ia, “Kapau ko e ʻAlo koe ʻoe ʻOtua, fekau ki he maka ni ke liliu ko e mā.”
And the devil said unto him, If thou be the Son of God, command this stone that it be made bread.
Pea leaange ʻa Sisu kiate ia, ʻo pehē, “Kuo tohi, ‘ʻE ʻikai moʻui ʻae tangata ʻi he mā pe, ka ʻi he folofola kotoa pē ʻae ʻOtua.’”
And Jesus answered him, saying, It is written, That man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word of God.
Pea naʻe ʻave ia ʻe he tēvolo ki he moʻunga māʻolunga, ʻo fakahā fakafokifā pe kiate ia ʻae ngaahi puleʻanga kotoa pē ʻo māmani.
And the devil, taking him up into an high mountain, shewed unto him all the kingdoms of the world in a moment of time.
Pea naʻe pehē ʻe he tēvolo kiate ia, “Te u ʻatu moʻou ʻae mālohi ni kotoa pē, mo hono nāunau: he kuo tuku mai ia kiate au; pea ʻoku ou foaki ia ko ʻeku faʻiteliha.
And the devil said unto him, All this power will I give thee, and the glory of them: for that is delivered unto me; and to whomsoever I will I give it.
Ko ia kapau te ke hū kiate au, ʻe ʻoʻou ia kotoa pē.”
If thou therefore wilt worship me, all shall be thine.
Pea leaange ʻa Sisu, ʻo ne pehē kiate ia, “Sētane, ke ke ʻalu ki hoku tuʻa; he kuo tohi, ‘Ke ke hū kia Sihova ko ho ʻOtua, pea ko ia pe te ke tauhi.’”
And Jesus answered and said unto him, Get thee behind me, Satan: for it is written, Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God, and him only shalt thou serve.
Pea ne ʻomi ia ki Selūsalema, ʻo ne tuku ia ki he tuʻa falelotu lahi, pea pehē kiate ia, “Kapau ko e ʻAlo koe ʻoe ʻOtua, fakatō koe ʻi heni ki lalo:
And he brought him to Jerusalem, and set him on a pinnacle of the temple, and said unto him, If thou be the Son of God, cast thyself down from hence:
He kuo tohi, ‘ʻE fekau ʻe ia ʻene kau ʻāngelo kiate koe, ke nau tauhiʻi koe;
For it is written, He shall give his angels charge over thee, to keep thee:
Pea, ‘Te nau hapahapai koe, telia naʻa touʻia ho vaʻe ʻi ha maka.’”
And in their hands they shall bear thee up, lest at any time thou dash thy foot against a stone.
Pea leaange ʻa Sisu, ʻo ne pehē kiate ia, “Ka kuo pehē, ‘ʻOua te ke ʻahiʻahi kia Sihova ko ho ʻOtua.’”
And Jesus answering said unto him, It is said, Thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God.
Pea kuo fakaʻosi ʻe he tēvolo ʻae ʻahiʻahi kotoa pē, naʻe ʻalu ia ʻiate ia ʻo fuoloa siʻi.
And when the devil had ended all the temptation, he departed from him for a season.
Pea foki atu ʻa Sisu ki Kāleli, ʻi he mālohi ʻoe Laumālie: pea naʻe mafola hono ongoongo ki he potu fonua ko ia kotoa pē.
And Jesus returned in the power of the Spirit into Galilee: and there went out a fame of him through all the region round about.
Pea ako ia ʻi honau ngaahi falelotu, pea fakamālō ai ʻae kakai fulipē.
And he taught in their synagogues, being glorified of all.
Pea haʻu ia ki Nāsaleti, ʻaia naʻe tupu ai ia: pea hū ia ki he falelotu ʻi he ʻaho Sāpate, ʻo hangē ko ʻene faʻa fai, pea tuʻu hake ke lautohi.
And he came to Nazareth, where he had been brought up: and, as his custom was, he went into the synagogue on the sabbath day, and stood up for to read.
Pea naʻe ʻatu kiate ia ʻae tohi ʻae palōfita ko ʻIsaia. Pea ʻi heʻene folahi ʻae tohi, naʻa ne ʻilo ʻae potu kuo tohi ai, ʻo pehē,
And there was delivered unto him the book of the prophet Esaias. And when he had opened the book, he found the place where it was written,

“ʻOku ʻiate au ʻae Laumālie ʻo Sihova, Koeʻuhi kuo ne fakanofo au ke u malangaʻaki ʻae ongoongolelei ki he masiva; Kuo ne fekau au ke fakamoʻui ʻae loto mafesi, Ke malangaʻaki ʻae huhuʻi ki he kau pōpula, Mo e fakaʻā ʻoe kui, Ke veteange ʻakinautolu kuo lavea,

The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he hath anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor; he hath sent me to heal the brokenhearted, to preach deliverance to the captives, and recovering of sight to the blind, to set at liberty them that are bruised,
Ke malangaʻaki ʻae taʻu lelei ʻo Sihova.”
To preach the acceptable year of the Lord.
Pea ne takai ʻe ia ʻae tohi, ʻo ʻange ki he tauhi, pea nofo hifo. Pea sio fakamamaʻu kiate ia ʻae mata ʻokinautolu kotoa pē naʻe ʻi he falelotu.
And he closed the book, and he gave it again to the minister, and sat down. And the eyes of all them that were in the synagogue were fastened on him.
Pea ne fua lea ia kiate kinautolu, “Kuo fakamoʻoni ʻi he ʻaho ni ʻae tohi ko eni ʻi homou telinga.”
And he began to say unto them, This day is this scripture fulfilled in your ears.
Pea naʻa nau fakamālō kotoa pē kiate ia, ʻonau ofo ʻi he ngaahi lea mālie naʻe ʻalu atu ʻi hono fofonga. Pea naʻa nau pehē, “ʻIkai ko e foha eni ʻo Siosefa?”
And all bare him witness, and wondered at the gracious words which proceeded out of his mouth. And they said, Is not this Joseph’s son?

Pea pehē ʻe ia kiate kinautolu, “Ka ko e moʻoni te mou lea ʻaki ʻae fakatātā ni kiate au, ‘Faitoʻo, fakamoʻui koe:’ pea ko ia kotoa pē kuo mau fanongo kuo fai ʻi Kapaneume, fai foki ʻi heni ʻi ho fonua.”
And he said unto them, Ye will surely say unto me this proverb, Physician, heal thyself: whatsoever we have heard done in Capernaum, do also here in thy country.
Pea pehē ʻe ia, “Ko e moʻoni ʻoku ou tala atu kiate kimoutolu, ʻOku ʻikai ha palōfita ʻe ʻofeina ʻi hono fonua.
And he said, Verily I say unto you, No prophet is accepted in his own country.

Ka ʻoku ou tala moʻoni atu kiate kimoutolu, naʻe tokolahi ʻae fefine kuo mate honau husepāniti ʻi ʻIsileli, ʻi he ngaahi ʻaho ʻo ʻIlaisiā, ʻi he lolotonga ʻae tāpuni ʻoe langi, ʻi he taʻu ʻe tolu mo e māhina ʻe ono, pea naʻe honge lahi ʻae fonua kotoa;
But I tell you of a truth, many widows were in Israel in the days of Elias, when the heaven was shut up three years and six months, when great famine was throughout all the land;
Ka naʻe ʻikai fekau ʻa ʻIlaisiā ki ha taha ʻiate kinautolu, ka ki he fefine kuo mate hono husepāniti ʻi Salepita ʻi Saitoni.
But unto none of them was Elias sent, save unto Sarepta, a city of Sidon, unto a woman that was a widow.
Pea naʻe tokolahi ʻae kilia ʻi ʻIsileli, ʻi he kuonga ʻo ʻIlaisiā ko e palōfita; ka naʻe ʻikai ke fakamaʻa ha taha ʻiate kinautolu, ka ko Neamani ko e Silia.”
And many lepers were in Israel in the time of Eliseus the prophet; and none of them was cleansed, saving Naaman the Syrian.
Pea ko kinautolu kotoa pē naʻe ʻi he falelotu, naʻa nau mātuʻaki lili ʻi heʻenau fanongo ki he ngaahi meʻa ni,
And all they in the synagogue, when they heard these things, were filled with wrath,
‌ʻO nau tutuʻu, pea kapusi ia kituaʻā kolo, ʻo tataki ia ki he matanga ʻoe moʻunga ʻaia naʻe tuʻu ai ʻenau kolo, koeʻuhi ke nau lī ia ʻi he lilifa ki lalo.
And rose up, and thrust him out of the city, and led him unto the brow of the hill whereon their city was built, that they might cast him down headlong.
Ka naʻe ʻalu ia mei honau lotolotonga, pea mole atu ia,
But he passing through the midst of them went his way,
‌ʻO ne ʻalu hifo ki Kapaneume, ko e kolo ʻo Kāleli, ʻo ne ako kiate kinautolu ʻi he ngaahi ʻaho Sāpate.
And came down to Capernaum, a city of Galilee, and taught them on the sabbath days.
Pea naʻa nau ofo ʻi heʻene akonaki he naʻe lea ia ʻi he mālohi.
And they were astonished at his doctrine: for his word was with power.
Pea naʻe ʻi he falelotu ʻae tangata, naʻe ʻiate ia ʻae laumālie ʻoe tēvolo ʻuli, pea naʻe kalanga ia, ʻo leʻo lahi,
And in the synagogue there was a man, which had a spirit of an unclean devil, and cried out with a loud voice,
‌ʻO pehē, “ʻE Sisu ʻo Nāsaleti, tuku ai pe; ko e hā ʻakimautolu kiate koe? Kuo ke haʻu ke fakaʻauha ʻakimautolu? ʻOku ou ʻilo koe; ko e tokotaha māʻoniʻoni ʻoe ʻOtua.”
Saying, Let us alone; what have we to do with thee, thou Jesus of Nazareth? art thou come to destroy us? I know thee who thou art; the Holy One of God.

Pea lolomi ia ʻe Sisu, ʻo pehē, “Ke ke fakalongo pe, pea ke haʻu kituʻa ʻiate ia.” Pea kuo lī ʻae tangata ʻe he tēvolo ki he haʻohaʻonga pea haʻu ia kituʻa ʻiate ia, pea naʻe ʻikai te ne fakamamahi kiate ia.
And Jesus rebuked him, saying, Hold thy peace, and come out of him. And when the devil had thrown him in the midst, he came out of him, and hurt him not.
Pea naʻa nau ofo lahi ai kotoa pē, ʻonau fepehēʻaki, “Ko e hā ʻae akonaki ni! He ʻoku ne fekau ʻi he pule mo e mālohi ki he kau laumālie ʻuli, pea ʻoku nau haʻu kituʻa.”
And they were all amazed, and spake among themselves, saying, What a word is this! for with authority and power he commandeth the unclean spirits, and they come out.
Pea naʻe mafola hono ongoongo ki he potu kotoa pē ʻoe fonua ko ia.
And the fame of him went out into every place of the country round about.
Pea naʻe tuʻu hake ia, mei he falelotu, ʻo hū ki he fale ʻo Saimone. Pea ko e faʻē ʻae uaifi ʻo Saimone kuo pukea ʻi he mofi lahi; pea naʻa nau kole kiate ia koeʻuhi ko ia.
And he arose out of the synagogue, and entered into Simon’s house. And Simon’s wife’s mother was taken with a great fever; and they besought him for her.
Pea naʻa ne tuʻu hake kiate ia, ʻo taʻofi ʻae mofi, pea mahuʻi ia: ka ka tuʻu leva ia, ʻo tauhi ʻakinautolu.
And he stood over her, and rebuked the fever; and it left her: and immediately she arose and ministered unto them.

Pea kuo tō ʻae laʻā, pea ko kinautolu kotoa pē naʻe ai haʻanau mahaki ʻi he mahaki kehekehe, naʻe ʻomi ʻakinautolu kiate ia; pea ne hilifaki hono nima kiate kinautolu taki taha, ʻo fakamoʻui ʻakinautolu.
Now when the sun was setting, all they that had any sick with divers diseases brought them unto him; and he laid his hands on every one of them, and healed them.
Pea haʻu kituʻa ʻae kau tēvolo mei he tokolahi, ʻonau kalanga, ʻo pehē, “Ko koe ʻae Kalaisi ko e ʻAlo ʻoe ʻOtua.” Pea ne lolomi ʻakinautolu ke ʻoua ʻe fakahā ʻoku nau ʻilo ia ko e Kalaisi.
And devils also came out of many, crying out, and saying, Thou art Christ the Son of God. And he rebuking them suffered them not to speak: for they knew that he was Christ.
Pea kuo ʻaho, pea ʻalu ia, ʻo nofo ʻi ha potu lala: pea kumi ia ʻe he kakai, ʻonau omi kiate ia, pea naʻa nau taʻofia ia, ke ʻoua naʻa ne ʻalu ʻiate kinautolu.
And when it was day, he departed and went into a desert place: and the people sought him, and came unto him, and stayed him, that he should not depart from them.
Ka naʻe pehē ʻe ia kiate kinautolu, “ʻOku totonu ke u malangaʻaki ʻae puleʻanga ʻoe ʻOtua ki he ngaahi kolo kehe foki he ko ia kuo fekau ai au.”
And he said unto them, I must preach the kingdom of God to other cities also: for therefore am I sent.
Pea malanga ʻe ia ʻi he ngaahi falelotu ʻo Kāleli.
And he preached in the synagogues of Galilee.
Pea pehē, ʻi heʻene tuʻu ʻi he matātahi ʻo Kenesaleti, naʻe lolofi mai kiate ia ʻae kakai ke fanongo ki he folofola ʻae ʻOtua.
And it came to pass, that, as the people pressed upon him to hear the word of God, he stood by the lake of Gennesaret,
Pea mamata ia ki he vaka ʻe ua ʻoku toka ʻi he veʻe ano: ka kuo ʻalu mei ai ʻae kau toutai ika, ʻonau fō honau ngaahi kupenga.
And saw two ships standing by the lake: but the fishermen were gone out of them, and were washing their nets.
Pea heka ia ki he vaka ʻe taha, ʻaia naʻe ʻo Saimone, pea ne kole kiate ia ke tukutuku siʻi mei ʻuta. Pea naʻe nofo hifo ia, ʻo akonaki ki he kakai mei he vaka.
And he entered into one of the ships, which was Simon’s, and prayed him that he would thrust out a little from the land. And he sat down, and taught the people out of the ship.
Pea kuo hili ʻene lea, pea pehē ʻe ia kia Saimone, “Maʻu atu ki he loloto, pea ʻaʻau homou ngaahi kupenga koeʻuhi kae fusi hake.”
Now when he had left speaking, he said unto Simon, Launch out into the deep, and let down your nets for a draught.
Pea lea ʻa Saimone, ʻo pehēange kiate ia, “ʻEiki, kuo mau ngāue ʻanepō ʻo ʻaho, ka naʻe ʻikai maʻu ha meʻa: ka ʻi hoʻo fekau te u ʻaʻau ʻae kupenga.”
And Simon answering said unto him, Master, we have toiled all the night, and have taken nothing: nevertheless at thy word I will let down the net.
Pea kuo nau fai ia, pea nau maʻu ʻae ngaahi ika ʻo lahi ʻaupito: pea kamata mahae honau kupenga.
And when they had this done, they inclosed a great multitude of fishes: and their net brake.
Pea nau taʻalo ki heʻenau kaunga toutai ika ʻi he vaka ʻe taha, ke nau haʻu ʻo tokoni ʻakinautolu. Pea naʻa nau omi, ʻo fakapito ʻae vaka fakatouʻosi, pea na kamata ngalo hifo.
And they beckoned unto their partners, which were in the other ship, that they should come and help them. And they came, and filled both the ships, so that they began to sink.
Pea kuo mamata ʻa Saimone Pita, pea fakatōmapeʻe ia ki he tui ʻo Sisu, ʻo ne pehē, “ʻE ʻEiki, ʻalu ʻiate au; he ko e tangata angahala au.”
When Simon Peter saw it, he fell down at Jesus’ knees, saying, Depart from me; for I am a sinful man, O Lord.
He naʻe ofo ia, mo kinautolu kotoa pē naʻe ʻiate ia, ʻi he ngaahi ika kuo maʻu:
For he was astonished, and all that were with him, at the draught of the fishes which they had taken:
Pea pehē foki ʻa Semisi, mo Sione ko e ongo foha ʻo Sepeti, ko e kaunga toutai mo Saimone. Pea pehē ʻe Sisu kia Saimone, “ʻOua ʻe manavahē; ngata heni te ke toutai tangata.”
And so was also James, and John, the sons of Zebedee, which were partners with Simon. And Jesus said unto Simon, Fear not; from henceforth thou shalt catch men.
Pea kuo ʻomi honau ongo vaka ki ʻuta, naʻa nau liʻaki kotoa pē, ʻo muimui kiate ia.
And when they had brought their ships to land, they forsook all, and followed him.

Pea naʻe lolotonga ʻene ʻi he kolo ʻe taha, pea vakai, ko e tangata kuo fonu ʻi he kilia: pea ne mamata kia Sisu, mo tō fakafoʻohifo, ʻo kole kiate ia, ʻo pehē, “ʻEiki, kapau ko ho loto ʻoku ke faʻa fakamaʻa au.”
And it came to pass, when he was in a certain city, behold a man full of leprosy: who seeing Jesus fell on his face, and besought him, saying, Lord, if thou wilt, thou canst make me clean.
Pea mafao ʻe ia hono nima, ʻo ala ki ai mo ne pehē, “Ko hoku loto: ke ke maʻa koe.” Pea mahuʻi leva ʻiate ia ʻae kilia.
And he put forth his hand, and touched him, saying, I will: be thou clean. And immediately the leprosy departed from him.

Pea ne fekau ia, “Ke ʻoua naʻa tala ki ha taha: kae ʻalu, ʻo fakahā koe ki he taulaʻeiki, mo ke ʻange koeʻuhi ko hoʻo fakamaʻa, ʻo fakatatau mo ia naʻe fekau ʻe Mōsese, ko e fakamoʻoni kiate kinautolu.”
And he charged him to tell no man: but go, and shew thyself to the priest, and offer for thy cleansing, according as Moses commanded, for a testimony unto them.
Ka naʻe ʻāsili ai ʻae mafola ʻa hono ongoongo: pea naʻe fakataha ʻae kakai tokolahi ʻaupito ke fanongo, pea koeʻuhi ke ne fakamoʻui ʻakinautolu ʻi honau ngaahi mahamahaki.
But so much the more went there a fame abroad of him: and great multitudes came together to hear, and to be healed by him of their infirmities.
Pea naʻe ʻalu ia mei ai ki he toafa, ʻo lotu ai.
And he withdrew himself into the wilderness, and prayed.

Pea pehē, ko e ʻaho ʻe taha, ʻi heʻene akonaki, naʻe nofo ai ʻae kau Fālesi mo e kau akonaki ʻi he fono, kuo nau omi mei he potu kakai kotoa pē ʻo Kāleli, mo Siutea, mo Selūsalema: pea naʻe ʻi ai ʻae mālohi ʻoe ʻEiki ke fakamoʻui ʻakinautolu.

And it came to pass on a certain day, as he was teaching, that there were Pharisees and doctors of the law sitting by, which were come out of every town of Galilee, and Judaea, and Jerusalem: and the power of the Lord was present to heal them.
Pea vakai, naʻe ʻomi ʻe he kau tangata ʻae tangata ʻi hono mohenga kuo pukea ʻi he mahaki tete: pea naʻa nau feinga pe fēfeeʻi hono lava mai ki loto, ke tuku ʻi hono ʻao.
And, behold, men brought in a bed a man which was taken with a palsy: and they sought means to bring him in, and to lay him before him.
Pea kuo ʻikai te nau ʻilo pe fēfeeʻi hono lava mai ki loto, koeʻuhi ko e kakai, naʻa nau ʻohake ia kituʻa fale, ʻo tukutuku hifo ia ʻi he ʻato ʻi he mohenga ki he haʻohaʻonga, ʻi he ʻao ʻo Sisu.
And when they could not find by what way they might bring him in because of the multitude, they went upon the housetop, and let him down through the tiling with his couch into the midst before Jesus.
Pea kuo mamata ʻe ia ki heʻenau tui, pea ne pehē kiate ia, “Tangata, kuo fakamolemole kiate koe hoʻo ngaahi angahala.”
And when he saw their faith, he said unto him, Man, thy sins are forgiven thee.
Pea fakakaukau leva ʻae kau tangata tohi mo e kau Fālesi, ʻonau pehē, “Ko hai eni ʻoku ne lea fie ʻOtua? Ko hai te ne faʻa fakamolemole ʻae angahala, ka ko e ʻOtua pe?”
And the scribes and the Pharisees began to reason, saying, Who is this which speaketh blasphemies? Who can forgive sins, but God alone?
Ka kuo ʻilo ʻe Sisu ʻenau mahalo, pea lea ia, ʻo pehēange kiate kinautolu, “Ko e hā ʻoku mou femahaloʻaki ai ʻi homou loto?
But when Jesus perceived their thoughts, he answering said unto them, What reason ye in your hearts?
He ʻoku faingofua ʻa fē, ke lea, ‘Kuo fakamolemole kiate koe hoʻo ngaahi angahala;’ pe ko e lea, ‘Tuʻu hake ʻo ʻalu?’
Whether is easier, to say, Thy sins be forgiven thee; or to say, Rise up and walk?

Ka koeʻuhi ke mou ʻilo ʻoku ʻi he Foha ʻoe tangata ʻae mālohi ʻi māmani ke fakamolemole ʻae angahala,” (pea pehē ʻe ia ki he mahaki tete,) “ʻOku ou pehē atu kiate koe, Tuʻu hake, ʻo toʻo ho mohenga, pea ke ke ʻalu ki ho fale.”
But that ye may know that the Son of man hath power upon earth to forgive sins, (he said unto the sick of the palsy,) I say unto thee, Arise, and take up thy couch, and go into thine house.
Pea naʻe tuʻu hake leva ia ʻi honau ʻao, pea ne toʻo mai ʻaia naʻe tokoto ai, ʻo ʻalu ki hono fale, mo fakamālō ki he ʻOtua.
And immediately he rose up before them, and took up that whereon he lay, and departed to his own house, glorifying God.
Pea nau ofo ai kotoa pē, mo nau fakamālō ki he ʻOtua, pea fonu ʻi he manavahē, ʻonau pehē, “Kuo tau mamata ʻi he ʻaho ni ki he ngaahi meʻa foʻou!”
And they were all amazed, and they glorified God, and were filled with fear, saying, We have seen strange things to day.
Pea hili ʻae ngaahi meʻa ni, pea ʻalu atu ia, ʻo ne mamata ki he tangata tānaki tukuhau, ko Livai hono hingoa, ʻoku nofo ia ʻi he tukuhauʻanga; pea ne pehē kiate ia, “Muimui ʻiate au.”
And after these things he went forth, and saw a publican, named Levi, sitting at the receipt of custom: and he said unto him, Follow me.
Pea tukuange ʻe ia ʻae meʻa kotoa pē, ʻo tuʻu hake, pea muimui ʻiate ia.
And he left all, rose up, and followed him.
Pea naʻe fai ʻe Livai ʻae kātoanga lahi kiate ia ʻi hono fale: pea naʻe nofo mo kinautolu ʻae kau tānaki tukuhau tokolahi, mo e kakai niʻihi.
And Levi made him a great feast in his own house: and there was a great company of publicans and of others that sat down with them.
Ka naʻe lāunga honau kau tangata tohi mo e kau Fālesi ki heʻene kau ākonga, ʻonau pehē, “Ko e hā ʻoku mou kai mo inu fakataha ai mo e kau tānaki tukuhau mo e angahala?”
But their scribes and Pharisees murmured against his disciples, saying, Why do ye eat and drink with publicans and sinners?
Pea leaange ʻa Sisu, ʻo pehē kiate kinautolu, “ʻOku ʻikai ʻaonga ʻae faitoʻo kiate kinautolu ʻoku mālōlō; ka ki he mahaki.
And Jesus answering said unto them, They that are whole need not a physician; but they that are sick.
Naʻe ʻikai te u haʻu ke ui ʻae māʻoniʻoni, ka ko e angahala ke fakatomala.”
I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.
Pea nau pehē kiate ia, “Ko e hā ʻoku faʻa ʻaukai mo lotu ai ʻae kau ākonga ʻa Sione, mo kinautolu foki ʻoe kau Fālesi; ka ʻoku kai mo inu ʻakinautolu ʻoku ʻoʻou.”
And they said unto him, Why do the disciples of John fast often, and make prayers, and likewise the disciples of the Pharisees; but thine eat and drink?
Pea pehē ʻe ia kiate kinautolu, “Te mou faʻa pule ke ʻaukai ʻae kāinga ʻoe tangata taʻane, ʻi he kei ʻiate kinautolu ʻae tangata taʻane?
And he said unto them, Can ye make the children of the bridechamber fast, while the bridegroom is with them?
Ka ʻe hoko ʻae ngaahi ʻaho ʻe ʻave ai ʻae tangata taʻane ʻiate kinautolu, pea ko e ngaahi ʻaho ko ia te nau toki ʻaukai ai.”
But the days will come, when the bridegroom shall be taken away from them, and then shall they fast in those days.

Pea lea ʻaki foki ʻe ia ʻae fakatātā kiate kinautolu; “ʻOku ʻikai ha taha te ne monomono ʻaki ʻae kofu motuʻa ha konga ʻoe kofu foʻou; ka pehē, ʻe hae ia ʻe he meʻa foʻou, kaeʻumaʻā ʻoku ʻikai fai tatau ʻae konga foʻou mo e motuʻa kofu.

And he spake also a parable unto them; No man putteth a piece of a new garment upon an old; if otherwise, then both the new maketh a rent, and the piece that was taken out of the new agreeth not with the old.
Pea ʻoku ʻikai ha taha te ne ʻutu ʻae uaine foʻou ki he ngaahi hina ʻoku motuʻa; telia naʻa hae ʻe he uaine foʻou ʻae ngaahi hina, pea tafe, pea maumau ʻae ngaahi hina.
And no man putteth new wine into old bottles; else the new wine will burst the bottles, and be spilled, and the bottles shall perish.
Kae ʻutu ʻae uaine foʻou ki he ngaahi hina foʻou; pea tolonga ai fakatouʻosi.
But new wine must be put into new bottles; and both are preserved.
‌ʻOku ʻikai foki ha tangata kuo inu ʻi he uaine motuʻa pea fili leva ia ki he uaine foʻou; he ʻoku ne pehē, ‘ʻOku lelei lahi ʻa e uaine motuʻa.’”
No man also having drunk old wine straightway desireth new: for he saith, The old is better.
Pea ko eni, naʻe ai ha Sāpate, naʻe ʻalu ia ʻi he ngaahi ngoue uite; pea toli ʻe heʻene kau ākonga ʻae fua ʻoe uite, ʻo momosi ʻi honau nima mo nau kai.
And it came to pass on the second sabbath after the first, that he went through the corn fields; and his disciples plucked the ears of corn, and did eat, rubbing them in their hands.
Pea naʻe pehē ʻe he niʻihi ʻoe Fālesi kiate kinautolu, “Ko e hā ʻoku mou fai ai ʻaia ʻoku ʻikai ngofua ke fai ʻi he ʻaho Sāpate?”
And certain of the Pharisees said unto them, Why do ye that which is not lawful to do on the sabbath days?
Pea leaange ʻa Sisu, ʻo pehē kiate kinautolu, “Naʻe ʻikai te mou lau ʻaia naʻe fai ʻe Tevita, ʻi heʻene fiekaia, mo kinautolu naʻe ʻiate ia;
And Jesus answering them said, Have ye not read so much as this, what David did, when himself was an hungred, and they which were with him;
‌ʻA ʻene hū ki he fale ʻoe ʻOtua, pea ne toʻo ʻo kai ʻae mā ʻoe ʻao, pea ʻange foki kiate kinautolu naʻe ʻiate ia; ʻaia ʻoku ʻikai ngofua ke kai ai ka ko e kau taulaʻeiki pe?”
How he went into the house of God, and did take and eat the shewbread, and gave also to them that were with him; which it is not lawful to eat but for the priests alone?
Mo ne pehē kiate kinautolu, “Ko e Foha ʻoe tangata ko e ʻEiki foki ia ʻoe Sāpate.”
And he said unto them, That the Son of man is Lord also of the sabbath.
Pea ʻi he hoko ki he Sāpate foki ʻe taha, naʻe hū ia ki he falelotu ʻo ako ai: pea naʻe ʻi ai ʻae tangata kuo mate hono nima toʻomataʻu.
And it came to pass also on another sabbath, that he entered into the synagogue and taught: and there was a man whose right hand was withered.
Pea lamasi ia ʻe he kau tangata tohi mo e kau Fālesi, pe te ne fakamoʻui ia ʻi he ʻaho Sāpate; koeʻuhi ke nau ʻilo ha meʻa ke talakoviʻi ai ia.
And the scribes and Pharisees watched him, whether he would heal on the sabbath day; that they might find an accusation against him.
Ka naʻe ʻilo ʻe ia ʻenau mahalo, pea ne pehē ki he tangata naʻe nima mate, “Tuʻu hake, ʻo tuʻu mai ki loto. Pea naʻe tuʻu hake ia, ʻo tuʻu ʻi ai.”
But he knew their thoughts, and said to the man which had the withered hand, Rise up, and stand forth in the midst. And he arose and stood forth.
Pea toki pehē atu ʻe Sisu kiate kinautolu, “Te u fehuʻi kiate kimoutolu ki he meʻa ʻe taha; Ko e hā ʻoku ngofua ke fai ʻi he ʻaho Sāpate, ko e lelei pe ko e kovi! Ko e fakamoʻui pe ko e tāmateʻi?”
Then said Jesus unto them, I will ask you one thing; Is it lawful on the sabbath days to do good, or to do evil? to save life, or to destroy it?
Pea naʻe vakai folia ʻe ia ʻakinautolu kotoa pē, pea pehē ʻe ia ki he tangata, “Mafao atu ho nima.” Pea ne fai ia: pea moʻui hono nima ʻo hangē ko hono nima ʻe taha.
And looking round about upon them all, he said unto the man, Stretch forth thy hand. And he did so: and his hand was restored whole as the other.
Ka naʻe mātuʻaki lili ʻakinautolu: ʻonau fakakaukau pe ko e hā te nau fai kia Sisu.
And they were filled with madness; and communed one with another what they might do to Jesus.
Pea pehē, ʻi he ngaahi ʻaho ko ia naʻe ʻalu hake ia ki ha moʻunga ke lotu, pea lotu ai pe ia ki he ʻOtua ʻi he pō ʻo ʻaho.
And it came to pass in those days, that he went out into a mountain to pray, and continued all night in prayer to God.
Pea kuo ʻaho hake, pea ne ui kiate ia ʻa ʻene kau ākonga; pea naʻa ne fili ʻiate kinautolu ʻae toko hongofulu ma toko ua, ʻaia foki naʻa ne fakahingoa ko e kau ʻaposetolo;
And when it was day, he called unto him his disciples: and of them he chose twelve, whom also he named apostles;
Ko Saimone, (naʻa ne fakahingoa ko Pita,) mo ʻAnitelū ko hono tokoua, mo Semisi, mo Sione, mo Filipe, mo Pātolomiu,
Simon, (whom he also named Peter,) and Andrew his brother, James and John, Philip and Bartholomew,
Mo Mātiu, mo Tōmasi, mo Semisi ko e foha ʻo ʻAlefiusi, mo Saimone ʻoku ui ko Selote,
Matthew and Thomas, James the son of Alphaeus, and Simon called Zelotes,
Mo Siutasi ko e tokoua ʻo Semisi, mo Siutasi ʻIsikaliote, ʻaia foki ko e lavaki.
And Judas the brother of James, and Judas Iscariot, which also was the traitor.

Pea naʻe ʻalu hifo ia mo kinautolu, ʻo tuʻu ʻi he potu tafangafanga, fakataha mo ʻene kau ākonga, pea naʻe haʻu ʻae kakai tokolahi ʻaupito mei Siutea kotoa pē mo Selūsalema, mo e matātahi ʻo Taia mo Saitoni, ke nau fanongo kiate ia, mo moʻui mei honau ngaahi mahaki;

And he came down with them, and stood in the plain, and the company of his disciples, and a great multitude of people out of all Judaea and Jerusalem, and from the sea coast of Tyre and Sidon, which came to hear him, and to be healed of their diseases;
Pea mo kinautolu naʻe mamahi ʻi he kau laumālie ʻuli: pea naʻe fakamoʻui ʻakinautolu.
And they that were vexed with unclean spirits: and they were healed.
Pea holi ʻae kakai kotoa pē ke nau ala kiate ia: he naʻe ʻalu ʻiate ia ʻae mālohi, ʻo fakamoʻui kotoa pē.
And the whole multitude sought to touch him: for there went virtue out of him, and healed them all.
Pea tangaki hake ʻe ia hono mata ki heʻene kau ākonga, ʻo ne pehē, “ʻOku monūʻia ʻakimoutolu ʻoku masiva; He ʻoku ʻomoutolu ʻae puleʻanga ʻoe ʻOtua.
And he lifted up his eyes on his disciples, and said, Blessed be ye poor: for yours is the kingdom of God.
“ʻOku monūʻia ʻakimoutolu ʻoku fiekaia ni: Koeʻuhi ʻe fakamākona ʻakimoutolu. ʻOku monūʻia ʻakimoutolu ʻoku tangi ni: He te mou kata.
Blessed are ye that hunger now: for ye shall be filled. Blessed are ye that weep now: for ye shall laugh.

“ʻOku monūʻia ʻakimoutolu ʻoka fehiʻa ʻae kakai kiate kimoutolu, Mo fakamavaheʻi ʻakimoutolu meiate kinautolu, ʻO taukae kiate kimoutolu, Pea lī kituʻa homou hingoa ʻo hangē ko e kovi, Koeʻuhi ko e Foha ʻoe tangata.
Blessed are ye, when men shall hate you, and when they shall separate you from their company, and shall reproach you, and cast out your name as evil, for the Son of man’s sake.
Mou fiefia ʻi he ʻaho ko ia, Pea hopohopo ʻi he fiefia: Vakai, he ʻoku lahi hoʻomou totongi ʻi he langi: He naʻe fai pehē ʻenau ngaahi tamai ki he kau palōfita.
Rejoice ye in that day, and leap for joy: for, behold, your reward is great in heaven: for in the like manner did their fathers unto the prophets.
“Kae malaʻia ʻakimoutolu ʻoku koloaʻia! He kuo mou maʻu hoʻomou fiemālie.
But woe unto you that are rich! for ye have received your consolation.
“ʻE malaʻia ʻakimoutolu ʻoku mākona! He te mou fiekaia. ʻE malaʻia ʻakimoutolu ʻoku kata ni! He te mou tangi mo tangilāulau.
Woe unto you that are full! for ye shall hunger. Woe unto you that laugh now! for ye shall mourn and weep.
“ʻE malaʻia ʻakimoutolu ʻoka lauʻi lelei ʻakimoutolu ʻe he kakai kotoa pē! He naʻe fai pehē ʻa ʻenau ngaahi tamai ki he kau palōfita kākā.
Woe unto you, when all men shall speak well of you! for so did their fathers to the false prophets.
“Ka ʻoku ou tala atu kiate kimoutolu ʻoku fanongo, ʻofa ki homou ngaahi fili, fai lelei kiate kinautolu ʻoku fehiʻa kiate kimoutolu.
But I say unto you which hear, Love your enemies, do good to them which hate you,
Tāpuakiʻi ʻakinautolu ʻoku kapeʻi ʻakimoutolu, pea hūfia ʻakinautolu ʻoku fakakoviʻi ʻakimoutolu.
Bless them that curse you, and pray for them which despitefully use you.
Pea ko ia ʻoku ne sipiʻi koe ʻi ho kouʻahe ʻe taha, fulihi kiate ia ho kouʻahe ʻe taha; pea mo ia ʻoku ne ʻave ho pulupulu, ʻoua naʻa taʻofi ʻene ʻave mo ho kofutuʻa.
And unto him that smiteth thee on the one cheek offer also the other; and him that taketh away thy cloak forbid not to take thy coat also.
Foaki kiate ia fulipē ʻoku kole kiate koe; pea ko ia ʻoku ne ʻave hoʻo koloa ʻoua naʻa toe kole ia.
Give to every man that asketh of thee; and of him that taketh away thy goods ask them not again.
Pea ko ia te mou loto ke fai ʻe he kakai kiate kimoutolu, ko ia pe foki te mou fai kiate kinautolu.
And as ye would that men should do to you, do ye also to them likewise.
“He kapau ʻoku mou ʻofa kiate kinautolu pe ʻoku ʻofa mai kiate kimoutolu, ko e hā ʻae fakafetaʻi ʻoku mou maʻu? He ʻoku ʻofa mai ʻae kau angahala kiate kinautolu ʻoku ʻofa ange kiate kinautolu.
For if ye love them which love you, what thank have ye? for sinners also love those that love them.
Pea kapau ʻoku mou fai lelei kiate kinautolu pe ʻoku fai lelei kiate kimoutolu, ko e hā ʻae fakafetaʻi ʻoku mou maʻu? He ʻoku fai pehē ʻe he kau angahala.
And if ye do good to them which do good to you, what thank have ye? for sinners also do even the same.
Pea kapau ʻoku mou ʻatu meʻa kiate kinautolu pe ʻoku mou ʻamanaki ke maʻu mei ai, ko e hā ʻae fakafetaʻi te mou maʻu? He ʻoku ʻatu meʻa ʻae kau angahala ki he kau angahala, ke toe maʻu hono tatau.
And if ye lend to them of whom ye hope to receive, what thank have ye? for sinners also lend to sinners, to receive as much again.

Ka mou ʻofa ki homou ngaahi fili, pea fai lelei, mo ʻatu meʻa, ʻi he taʻeʻamanaki ke toe maʻu; pea ʻe lahi ai hoʻomou totongi pea ʻe ui ʻakimoutolu ko e fānau ʻae Fungani Māʻolunga: he ʻoku angalelei ia ki he taʻefakafetaʻi pea mo e kovi.

But love ye your enemies, and do good, and lend, hoping for nothing again; and your reward shall be great, and ye shall be the children of the Highest: for he is kind unto the unthankful and to the evil.
Ko ia mou manavaʻofa, ʻo hangē foki ko e manavaʻofa ʻa hoʻomou Tamai.
Be ye therefore merciful, as your Father also is merciful.
“ʻOua ʻe fakamaau, pea ʻe ʻikai fakamaauʻi ʻakimoutolu: ʻoua naʻa fakahalaia, pea ʻe ʻikai fakahalaia ʻakimoutolu: mou fakamolemole, pea ʻe fakamolemolea ʻakimoutolu:
Judge not, and ye shall not be judged: condemn not, and ye shall not be condemned: forgive, and ye shall be forgiven:

Foaki, pea ʻe foaki ia kiate kimoutolu; ko e fua lahi, kuo faʻo lolo hifo, ʻo lulu fakataha, pea fonu mahuohua, ʻe ʻatu ki homou fatafata. He ko e fuofua ko ia te mou fua ʻaki, ʻe toe fua ʻaki ia kiate kimoutolu.”

Give, and it shall be given unto you; good measure, pressed down, and shaken together, and running over, shall men give into your bosom. For with the same measure that ye mete withal it shall be measured to you again.
Pea naʻa ne lea ʻaki ʻae fakatātā kiate kinautolu, “ʻE faʻa taki ʻe he kui ʻae kui? ʻIkai te na tō fakatouʻosi ki he luo?”
And he spake a parable unto them, Can the blind lead the blind? shall they not both fall into the ditch?
‌ʻOku ʻikai lahi hake ʻae ākonga ʻi heʻene akonaki: ka ko ia kotoa pē ʻoku haohaoa ʻe hangē ia ko ʻene akonaki.
The disciple is not above his master: but every one that is perfect shall be as his master.
“Pea ko e hā ʻoku ke tokanga ai ki he malamalaʻi ʻakau ʻi he mata ʻo ho kāinga, ka ʻoku ʻikai te ke ʻilo ʻae fuʻu ʻakau ʻoku ʻi ho mata?
And why beholdest thou the mote that is in thy brother’s eye, but perceivest not the beam that is in thine own eye?

Pea ʻe fēfē haʻo faʻa pehē ki ho kāinga, ‘Kāinga, tuku mai ke u toʻo ʻae malamalaʻi ʻakau ʻoku ʻi ho mata,’ ka ʻoku ʻikai te ke ʻilo ʻae fuʻu ʻakau ʻoku ʻi ho mata? Ko e mālualoi koe, tomuʻa lī ʻae fuʻu ʻakau mei ho mata, pea te ke toki ʻilo totonu ke toʻo mai ʻae malamalaʻi ʻakau mei he mata ʻo ho kāinga.

Either how canst thou say to thy brother, Brother, let me pull out the mote that is in thine eye, when thou thyself beholdest not the beam that is in thine own eye? Thou hypocrite, cast out first the beam out of thine own eye, and then shalt thou see clearly to pull out the mote that is in thy brother’s eye.
“He ʻoku ʻikai ha ʻakau lelei ʻe tupu ai ʻae fua kovi; pe ha ʻakau kovi ʻe tupu ai ʻae fua lelei.
For a good tree bringeth not forth corrupt fruit; neither doth a corrupt tree bring forth good fruit.
He ʻoku ʻilo ʻae ʻakau kotoa pē ʻi hono fua ʻoʻona. He ʻoku ʻikai toli ʻe he kakai ʻae fiki ʻi he ʻakau talatala, pe ko e fua ʻoe vaine ʻi he talatalaʻāmoa.
For every tree is known by his own fruit. For of thorns men do not gather figs, nor of a bramble bush gather they grapes.

‌ʻOku ʻomi ʻe he tangata angalelei ʻaia ʻoku lelei mei he koloa lelei ʻi hono loto; pea ʻoku ʻomi ʻe he tangata angakovi ʻaia ʻoku kovi mei he koloa kovi ʻi hono loto: he ʻoku lea ʻa hono ngutu mei he meʻa lahi ʻoe loto.

A good man out of the good treasure of his heart bringeth forth that which is good; and an evil man out of the evil treasure of his heart bringeth forth that which is evil: for of the abundance of the heart his mouth speaketh.
“Pea ko e hā ʻoku mou ui ai au, ‘ʻEiki, ʻEiki,’ kae ʻikai fai ʻae ngaahi meʻa ʻoku ou tala?
And why call ye me, Lord, Lord, and do not the things which I say?
Pea ko ia fulipē ʻoku haʻu kiate au, ʻo fanongo ki heʻeku ngaahi lea, mo fai ki ai, te u fakahā kiate kimoutolu hono tatau:
Whosoever cometh to me, and heareth my sayings, and doeth them, I will shew you to whom he is like:

‌ʻOku tatau ia mo e tangata naʻe langa ʻae fale, pea keli māʻulalo, ʻo ne ai hono tuʻunga ki he funga maka; pea ʻi he tupu ʻae vaitafe, pea ʻoho mālohi ʻae vai ki he fale ko ia, naʻe ʻikai ngaue ia; he naʻe fokotuʻu ia ki he maka.

He is like a man which built an house, and digged deep, and laid the foundation on a rock: and when the flood arose, the stream beat vehemently upon that house, and could not shake it: for it was founded upon a rock.

Ka ko ia ʻoku fanongo, kae ʻikai fai ki ai, ʻoku tatau ia mo e tangata naʻe langa ʻae fale ʻi he kelekele taʻehatuʻunga; pea naʻe ʻoho mālohi ʻae vai ki ai, pea holo leva ia; pea ko e maumau ʻoe fale ko ia ko e meʻa lahi.”

But he that heareth, and doeth not, is like a man that without a foundation built an house upon the earth; against which the stream did beat vehemently, and immediately it fell; and the ruin of that house was great.
Pea kuo fakaʻosi ʻe ia ʻa ʻene tala kotoa pē ʻi he ʻao ʻoe kakai, pea ʻalu ia ki Kapaneume.
Now when he had ended all his sayings in the audience of the people, he entered into Capernaum.
Pea naʻe mahaki, ʻo mei mate ʻae tamaioʻeiki ʻae ʻeikitau ʻe taha, ʻaia naʻe ʻofa lahi ai ia.
And a certain centurion’s servant, who was dear unto him, was sick, and ready to die.
Pea kuo fanongo ia kia Sisu, pea ne fekau ʻae kau mātuʻa ʻi he kakai Siu, ke fakakolekole kiate ia ke ne haʻu ʻo fakamoʻui ʻa ʻene tamaioʻeiki.
And when he heard of Jesus, he sent unto him the elders of the Jews, beseeching him that he would come and heal his servant.
Pea kuo nau omi kia Sisu, pea nau kole fakamātoato kiate ia, ʻo pehē, “ʻOku ʻaonga ia te ke fai ki ai ʻae meʻa ni:
And when they came to Jesus, they besought him instantly, saying, That he was worthy for whom he should do this:
He ʻoku ʻofa ia ki hotau kakai, pea ko ia ia ne langa ʻae falelotu moʻomautolu.”
For he loveth our nation, and he hath built us a synagogue.

Pea ʻalu ʻa Sisu mo kinautolu. Pea kuo hoko ia ʻo vāofi mo e fale, pea fekau ʻe he ʻeikitau ʻa hono kāinga, ke lea ʻo pehē kiate ia, “ʻEiki, ʻoua naʻa ke ongosia ange koe: he ʻoku ʻikai te u ʻaonga ke ke hū ki hoku fale:

Then Jesus went with them. And when he was now not far from the house, the centurion sent friends to him, saying unto him, Lord, trouble not thyself: for I am not worthy that thou shouldest enter under my roof:
Pea naʻe ʻikai te u mahalo ʻoku taau mo au ke u ʻalu atu kiate koe: ka ke fai haʻo lea, pea ʻe moʻui ai ʻeku tamaioʻeiki.
Wherefore neither thought I myself worthy to come unto thee: but say in a word, and my servant shall be healed.

He ko au ko e tangata puleʻia foki, ka ʻoku ai ʻae kautau ʻoku ou puleʻi pea ʻoku ou pehē ki ha taha, ‘ʻAlu,’ pea ʻalu ia; pea ki ha taha, ‘Haʻu,’ pea haʻu ia; pea ki heʻeku tamaioʻeiki, ‘Fai eni,’ pea ʻoku ne fai ia.
For I also am a man set under authority, having under me soldiers, and I say unto one, Go, and he goeth; and to another, Come, and he cometh; and to my servant, Do this, and he doeth it.

Pea ofo ʻa Sisu kiate ia, ʻi heʻene fanongo ki he ngaahi meʻa ni, pea tafoki ia, ʻo ne pehē ki he kakai naʻe muimui ʻiate ia, “ʻOku ou tala atu kiate kimoutolu, Naʻa mo ʻIsileli, ʻoku ʻikai te u ʻilo ai ha tui ʻe pehē ni hono lahi.”
When Jesus heard these things, he marvelled at him, and turned him about, and said unto the people that followed him, I say unto you, I have not found so great faith, no, not in Israel.
Pea liu atu ki he fale ʻakinautolu naʻe fekau, ʻonau ʻilo ʻae tamaioʻeiki naʻe mahaki kuo moʻui ia.
And they that were sent, returning to the house, found the servant whole that had been sick.
Pea ʻi he ʻaho naʻa na feholoi, naʻe ʻalu ia ki he kolo naʻe ui ko Neini: pea naʻe ʻalu mo ia ʻa ʻene kau ākonga tokolahi, mo e fuʻu kakai.
And it came to pass the day after, that he went into a city called Nain; and many of his disciples went with him, and much people.

Pea kuo ofi ia ki he matapā ʻoe kolo, pea vakai, naʻe fata mai kituaʻā ʻae tangata mate, ko e tama pe taha ia ʻa ʻene faʻē, pea ko e fefine ia kuo mate hono husepāniti: pea naʻe ʻiate ia ʻae kakai tokolahi ʻoe kolo.
Now when he came nigh to the gate of the city, behold, there was a dead man carried out, the only son of his mother, and she was a widow: and much people of the city was with her.
Pea kuo mamata ki ai ʻae ʻEiki, pea manavaʻofa ia kiate ia, ʻo ne pehē ki ai, “ʻOua ʻe tangi.”
And when the Lord saw her, he had compassion on her, and said unto her, Weep not.
Pea haʻu ia ʻo ala ki he fata: pea tuʻu pe ʻae kau fata. Pea pehē ʻe ia, “Talavou, ʻoku ou pehē kiate koe, Tuʻu hake.”
And he came and touched the bier: and they that bare him stood still. And he said, Young man, I say unto thee, Arise.
Pea nofo hake ia ʻaia naʻe mate, ʻo kamata lea. Pea ne ʻatu ia ki heʻene faʻē.
And he that was dead sat up, and began to speak. And he delivered him to his mother.
Pea pukea kotoa pē ʻi he manavahē: pea nau fakamālō ki he ʻOtua, ʻo pehē, “Kuo tuʻu hake ʻae palōfita lahi ʻiate kitautolu;” pea, “Kuo ʻaʻahi ʻae ʻOtua ki hono kakai.”
And there came a fear on all: and they glorified God, saying, That a great prophet is risen up among us; and, That God hath visited his people.
Pea naʻe mafola ʻa hono ongoongo ni ʻi Siutea kotoa pē, pea mo e potu fonua kotoa pē ko ia.
And this rumour of him went forth throughout all Judaea, and throughout all the region round about.
Pea naʻe fakahā ʻe he kau ākonga ʻa Sione kiate ia ʻae ngaahi meʻa ni kotoa pē.
And the disciples of John shewed him of all these things.
