For all these have of their abundance cast in unto the offerings of God: but she of her penury hath cast in all the living that she had.
Pea ʻi he lea ʻae niʻihi ki he falelotu lahi, ki hono teungaʻaki ʻae ngaahi maka lelei mo e ngaahi meʻa foaki, ne pehē ʻe ia,
And as some spake of the temple, how it was adorned with goodly stones and gifts, he said,
“Ko e ngaahi meʻa ʻoku mou mamata ki ai ni, ʻe hoko ʻae ngaahi ʻaho ʻe ʻikai mahili ai ha maka ki ha maka, ka ʻe laku kotoa pē ki lalo.”
As for these things which ye behold, the days will come, in the which there shall not be left one stone upon another, that shall not be thrown down.
Pea naʻa nau fehuʻi kiate ia, ʻo pehē, “ʻEiki, ʻe hoko afe ʻae ngaahi meʻa ni? Pea ko e hā ʻae fakaʻilonga ʻoka hoko ʻae ngaahi meʻa ni?”
And they asked him, saying, Master, but when shall these things be? and what sign will there be when these things shall come to pass?
Pea pehē ʻe ia, “Vakai, telia naʻa kākaaʻi ʻakimoutolu: koeʻuhi ʻe haʻu ʻae tokolahi ʻi hoku hingoa ʻonau pehē, ‘Ko au ia;’ pea ‘ʻOku ofi mai ʻae ʻaho:’ ko ia ʻoua naʻa mou muimui kiate kinautolu.
And he said, Take heed that ye be not deceived: for many shall come in my name, saying, I am Christ; and the time draweth near: go ye not therefore after them.
Ka ʻoka mou ka fanongo ki he ngaahi tau mo e ngaahi maveuveu, ʻoua naʻa mou ilifia: koeʻuhi ʻe tomuʻa hoko ʻae ngaahi meʻa ni; ka ʻe ʻikai vave ʻae ngataʻanga.”
But when ye shall hear of wars and commotions, be not terrified: for these things must first come to pass; but the end is not by and by.
Pea toki pehē ʻe ia kiate kinautolu, “ʻE tuʻu hake ʻae kakai ki he kakai, mo e puleʻanga ki he puleʻanga;
Then said he unto them, Nation shall rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom:
Pea ʻe hoko ʻae ngaahi mofuike lahi ʻi he potu kehekehe, mo e honge, mo e ngaahi mahaki lahi; pea ʻe hā mai mei he langi ʻae ngaahi meʻa fakailifia mo e ngaahi fakaʻilonga lahi.
And great earthquakes shall be in divers places, and famines, and pestilences; and fearful sights and great signs shall there be from heaven.

Kae teʻeki ai ke hoko eni, te nau pukea ʻakimoutolu, mo fakatangaʻi, mo tukuange ʻakimoutolu ki he ngaahi falelotu, mo e ngaahi fale fakapōpula, ʻonau ʻomi ʻakimoutolu ki he ʻao ʻoe ngaahi tuʻi mo e pule, koeʻuhi ko hoku hingoa.
But before all these, they shall lay their hands on you, and persecute you, delivering you up to the synagogues, and into prisons, being brought before kings and rulers for my name’s sake.
Pea ʻe hoko ia ko e fakamoʻoni kiate kimoutolu.
And it shall turn to you for a testimony.
Ko ia ke fakapapau homou loto, ke ʻoua naʻa tomuʻa fakakaukau ʻaia te mou tali ʻaki:
Settle it therefore in your hearts, not to meditate before what ye shall answer:
He te u foaki kiate kimoutolu ʻae ngutu mo e poto, ʻe ʻikai faʻa tali pe taʻofia ʻe homou ngaahi fili kotoa pē.
For I will give you a mouth and wisdom, which all your adversaries shall not be able to gainsay nor resist.
Ka ʻe lavakiʻi ʻakimoutolu ʻe he mātuʻa, mo e tokoua, mo e kāinga, mo e kaumeʻa; pea te nau tāmateʻi homou niʻihi.
And ye shall be betrayed both by parents, and brethren, and kinsfolks, and friends; and some of you shall they cause to be put to death.
Pea ʻe fehiʻanekina ʻakimoutolu ʻi he kakai kotoa pē koeʻuhi ko hoku hingoa.
And ye shall be hated of all men for my name’s sake.
Ka ʻe ʻikai mole ha tuʻoni louʻulu ʻi homou ʻulu.
But there shall not an hair of your head perish.
Mou maʻu ʻi hoʻomou faʻa kātaki ʻa homou laumālie.
In your patience possess ye your souls.
“Pea ʻoka mou ka mamata ki he kāpui ʻo Selūsalema ʻaki ʻae ngaahi matatau, mou toki ʻilo kuo ofi hono fakaʻauha.
And when ye shall see Jerusalem compassed with armies, then know that the desolation thereof is nigh.
Pea tuku ke toki feholaki ai ki he ngaahi moʻunga ʻakinautolu ʻoku ʻi Siutea; pea ko kinautolu ʻoku ʻi kolo ke nau ʻalu atu; pea ʻoua naʻa hū ki ai ʻakinautolu ʻoku nofo ʻi he tukuʻuta.
Then let them which are in Judaea flee to the mountains; and let them which are in the midst of it depart out; and let not them that are in the countries enter thereinto.
He ko e ‘ngaahi ʻaho eni ʻoe totongi,’ koeʻuhi ke fakamoʻoni ʻae meʻa kotoa pē kuo tohi.
For these be the days of vengeance, that all things which are written may be fulfilled.
Ka ʻe malaʻia ʻakinautolu ʻe feitama, mo kinautolu ʻe toutama, ʻi he ngaahi ʻaho ko ia! Koeʻuhi ʻe ai ʻae mamahi lahi ki he fonua, mo e houhau ki he kakai ni.
But woe unto them that are with child, and to them that give suck, in those days! for there shall be great distress in the land, and wrath upon this people.
Pea ʻe tō ʻakinautolu ʻi he mata ʻoe heletā, pea ʻe taki pōpula ki he puleʻanga kotoa pē: pea ʻe malaki hifo ʻa Selūsalema ʻe he kakai Senitaile, kaeʻoua ke kakato ʻae kuonga ʻoe kakai Senitaile.
And they shall fall by the edge of the sword, and shall be led away captive into all nations: and Jerusalem shall be trodden down of the Gentiles, until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled.
“Pea ʻe ai ʻae ngaahi fakaʻilonga ʻi he laʻā, mo e māhina, mo e ngaahi fetuʻu; pea ʻe ʻi he māmani ʻae mamahi ʻoe ngaahi kakai, mo e puputuʻu, koeʻuhi ko e ʻuʻulu ʻae tahi mo e ngaahi peau:
And there shall be signs in the sun, and in the moon, and in the stars; and upon the earth distress of nations, with perplexity; the sea and the waves roaring;
Ka ʻe mole ʻae loto ʻoe kakai ʻi he manavahē, mo tuʻotuʻatamaki ki he ngaahi meʻa ʻe hoko ki māmani: koeʻuhi ʻe ngalulululu ʻae ngaahi mālohi ʻoe langi.
Men’s hearts failing them for fear, and for looking after those things which are coming on the earth: for the powers of heaven shall be shaken.
Pea te nau toki mamata ki he Foha ʻoe tangata ʻoku haʻu ʻi he ngaahi ʻao, mo e mālohi mo e nāunau lahi.
And then shall they see the Son of man coming in a cloud with power and great glory.
Pea ʻi he kamata hoko mai ʻae ngaahi meʻa ni, mou sio hake, pea hanga hake homou ʻulu; he ʻoku ofi mai homou huhuʻi.”
And when these things begin to come to pass, then look up, and lift up your heads; for your redemption draweth nigh.
Pea naʻe lea ʻaki ʻe ia ʻae fakatātā kiate kinautolu; “Vakai ki he ʻakau ko e fiki, pea mo e ngaahi ʻakau kotoa pē;
And he spake to them a parable; Behold the fig tree, and all the trees;
‌ʻOka tupu hono muka, ʻoku mou mamata, pea mou ʻilo ai ʻoku ofi mai ʻae faʻahitaʻu mafana.
When they now shoot forth, ye see and know of your own selves that summer is now nigh at hand.
Pea ʻe pehē foki ʻakimoutolu, ʻoka mou ka mamata ki he hoko ʻoe ngaahi meʻa ni, mou ʻilo ʻoku ofi mai ʻae puleʻanga ʻoe ʻOtua.
So likewise ye, when ye see these things come to pass, know ye that the kingdom of God is nigh at hand.
“Ko e moʻoni ʻoku ou tala kiate kimoutolu, ʻE ʻikai mole ʻae toʻutangata ni, kaeʻoua ke fakamoʻoni kotoa pē.
Verily I say unto you, This generation shall not pass away, till all be fulfilled.
‌ʻE mole ʻae langi mo māmani; ka ʻe ʻikai mole ʻa ʻeku ngaahi lea.
Heaven and earth shall pass away: but my words shall not pass away.
“Kae vakai kiate kimoutolu, telia naʻa ʻiloange kuo taʻomia homou loto ʻi he kai fekinaki, mo e kona, mo e tokanga ki he moʻui ni, pea hoko fakafokifā ai ʻae ʻaho ko ia kiate kimoutolu.
And take heed to yourselves, lest at any time your hearts be overcharged with surfeiting, and drunkenness, and cares of this life, and so that day come upon you unawares.
Koeʻuhi ʻe hoko ia ʻo hangē ko e hele kiate kinautolu kotoa pē ʻoku nau nofo ʻi he funga ʻo māmani fulipē.
For as a snare shall it come on all them that dwell on the face of the whole earth.
Ko ia mou leʻo, pea lotu maʻuaipē, koeʻuhi ke mou ʻaonga ke hao mei he ngaahi meʻa ni kotoa pē ʻe hoko, pea ke tutuʻu ʻi he ʻao ʻoe Foha ʻoe tangata.”
Watch ye therefore, and pray always, that ye may be accounted worthy to escape all these things that shall come to pass, and to stand before the Son of man.
Pea naʻe ako ia ʻi he ʻaho ʻi he falelotu lahi; pea ʻi he pō, naʻa ne ʻalu kituaʻā ʻo nofo ʻi he moʻunga ʻoku ui ko ʻOlive.
And in the day time he was teaching in the temple; and at night he went out, and abode in the mount that is called the mount of Olives.
Pea naʻe haʻu hengihengi ʻae kakai kotoa pē kiate ia ʻi he falelotu lahi, ke nau fanongo kiate ia.
And all the people came early in the morning to him in the temple, for to hear him.
Pea naʻe ofi mai ʻae kātoanga ʻoe mā taʻemeʻafakatupu, ʻaia ʻoku ui ko e Lakaatu.
Now the feast of unleavened bread drew nigh, which is called the Passover.
Pea naʻe fifili ʻe he kau taulaʻeiki lahi mo e kau tangata tohi pe fēfeeʻi ʻenau tāmateʻi ia; ka naʻa nau manavahē ki he kakai.
And the chief priests and scribes sought how they might kill him; for they feared the people.
Pea hū ai ʻa Sētane kia Siutasi naʻe hingoa ko ʻIsikaliote, ko e taha ia ʻi he toko hongofulu ma toko ua.
Then entered Satan into Judas surnamed Iscariot, being of the number of the twelve.
Pea ʻalu ai ia, ʻonau alea mo e kau taulaʻeiki lahi mo e kau matāpule, pe fēfē ʻene lavakiʻi ia kiate kinautolu.
And he went his way, and communed with the chief priests and captains, how he might betray him unto them.
Pea naʻa nau fiefia, ʻo alea fakapapau ke ʻatu ha paʻanga kiate ia.
And they were glad, and covenanted to give him money.
Pea loto ia ki ai ʻo ne lamasi ke tuʻumālie ʻene lavaki ia kiate kinautolu ʻi he ʻikai ʻi ai ha kakai.
And he promised, and sought opportunity to betray him unto them in the absence of the multitude.
Pea hokosia ʻae ʻaho ʻoe mā taʻemeʻafakatupu, ʻaia ʻoku totonu ke tāmateʻi ai ʻa e feilaulau ʻoe Lakaatu.
Then came the day of unleavened bread, when the passover must be killed.
Pea fekauʻi ʻe ia ʻa Pita mo Sione, ʻo pehē, “Mo ō, ʻo teuteu ʻa e feilaulau ʻoe Lakaatu maʻatautolu, koeʻuhi ke tau kai.”
And he sent Peter and John, saying, Go and prepare us the passover, that we may eat.
Pea naʻa na pehē kiate ia, “Ko e potu fē ʻoku ke loto ke ma teuteu ai?”
And they said unto him, Where wilt thou that we prepare?
Pea pehē ʻe ia kiate kinaua, “Vakai, ʻi hoʻomo hū ki he kolo, te mo fetaulaki mo e tangata ʻoku ne fua ʻae hina vai; mo muimui ʻiate ia ki he fale ʻe hū ia ki ai.
And he said unto them, Behold, when ye are entered into the city, there shall a man meet you, bearing a pitcher of water; follow him into the house where he entereth in.
Pea mo pehē ki he ʻeiki ʻoe fale, ‘ʻOku pehē mai ʻae ʻEiki kiate koe, “Kofaʻā ia ʻae potu te mau kai ai ʻa e feilaulau ʻoe Lakaatu mo ʻeku kau ākonga?”’
And ye shall say unto the goodman of the house, The Master saith unto thee, Where is the guestchamber, where I shall eat the passover with my disciples?
Pea ʻe fakahā ʻe ia kiate kimoua ʻae potu lahi ʻi ʻolunga kuo teuʻi: pea mo teuteu ai.”
And he shall shew you a large upper room furnished: there make ready.
Pea naʻa na ō, ʻo na ʻilo ʻo hangē ko ʻene lea kiate kinaua; pea naʻa na teuteu ʻa e feilaulau ʻoe Lakaatu.
And they went, and found as he had said unto them: and they made ready the passover.
Pea kuo hokosia ʻae feituʻu efiafi, pea nofo hifo ia, mo e kau ʻaposetolo ʻe toko hongofulu ma toko ua.
And when the hour was come, he sat down, and the twelve apostles with him.
Pea pehē ʻe ia kiate kinautolu, “Kuo u holi ʻi he holi lahi, ke tau kai mo kimoutolu ʻa e feilaulau ʻoe Lakaatu ni ʻi he teʻeki ai te u mate.
And he said unto them, With desire I have desired to eat this passover with you before I suffer:
He ʻoku ou tala atu kiate kimoutolu. ʻE ʻikai te u toe kai ia, kaeʻoua ke fakamoʻoni ia ʻi he puleʻanga ʻoe ʻOtua.”
For I say unto you, I will not any more eat thereof, until it be fulfilled in the kingdom of God.
Pea toʻo ʻe ia ʻae ipu, ʻo ne fakafetaʻi, ʻo pehē, “Toʻo eni, ʻo tufaki kiate kimoutolu:
And he took the cup, and gave thanks, and said, Take this, and divide it among yourselves:
He ʻoku ou tala atu kiate kimoutolu, ʻE ʻikai te u inu ʻi he fua ʻoe vaine, kaeʻoua ke hokosia ʻae puleʻanga ʻoe ʻOtua.”
For I say unto you, I will not drink of the fruit of the vine, until the kingdom of God shall come.
Pea toʻo ʻe ia ʻae mā, ʻo ne fakafetaʻi, mo tofitofi ia, ʻo ne ʻatu kiate kinautolu, ʻo pehē, “Ko hoku sino eni, ʻaia kuo foaki koeʻuhi ko kimoutolu: fai eni ʻi he fakamanatu kiate au.”
And he took bread, and gave thanks, and brake it, and gave unto them, saying, This is my body which is given for you: this do in remembrance of me.
Pea hili ʻae ʻohomohe naʻetoʻo fokiʻe ia ʻae ipu, ʻo pehē, “Ko e ipu ni ko e fuakava foʻou ʻi hoku toto, ʻaia ʻoku lilingi koeʻuhi ko kimoutolu.
Likewise also the cup after supper, saying, This cup is the new testament in my blood, which is shed for you.
“Kae vakai, ko e nima ʻo ia ʻoku ne lavakiʻi au, ʻoku ʻiate au ʻi he keinangaʻanga.
But, behold, the hand of him that betrayeth me is with me on the table.
Pea ko e moʻoni ʻoku ʻalu ʻae Foha ʻoe tangata, ʻo hangē ko ia kuo tuʻutuʻuni: ka ʻe malaʻia ʻae tangata ko ia te ne lavakiʻi ia!”
And truly the Son of man goeth, as it was determined: but woe unto that man by whom he is betrayed!
Pea naʻa nau kamata fakafefehuʻiʻaki ʻiate kinautolu, pe ko hai ia ʻiate kinautolu ʻe fai ʻae meʻa ni.
And they began to enquire among themselves, which of them it was that should do this thing.
Pea naʻe ai ʻae kikihi foki ʻiate kinautolu, pe ko hai ʻiate kinautolu ʻe lahi.
And there was also a strife among them, which of them should be accounted the greatest.
Pea pehē ʻe ia kiate kinautolu, “Ko e ngaahi tuʻi ʻoe Senitaile ʻoku nau puleʻi ʻakinautolu: pea ko kinautolu ʻoku pule kakaha, ʻoku nau ui ʻakinautolu ‘ko e angalelei.’
And he said unto them, The kings of the Gentiles exercise lordship over them; and they that exercise authority upon them are called benefactors.
Ka ʻe ʻikai pehē ʻiate kimoutolu: ka ko ia ʻoku lahi ʻiate kimoutolu, tuku ke tatau ia mo e ki mui; pea mo ia ʻoku pule, ke tatau mo ia ʻoku tauhi.
But ye shall not be so: but he that is greatest among you, let him be as the younger; and he that is chief, as he that doth serve.
He ko hai ʻoku lahi, ko ia ʻoku ne nofo ʻo kai, pe ko ia ʻoku ne tauhi? ʻIkai ko ia ʻoku nofo ʻo kai? Ka ʻoku ou ʻiate kimoutolu ʻo hangē ko ia ʻoku tauhi.
For whether is greater, he that sitteth at meat, or he that serveth? is not he that sitteth at meat? but I am among you as he that serveth.
“Ko kimoutolu ia kuo nofomaʻu mo au, ʻi hoku ngaahi ʻahiʻahi.
Ye are they which have continued with me in my temptations.
Pea ʻoku ou tuʻutuʻuni kiate kimoutolu ha puleʻanga, ʻo hangē ko e tuʻutuʻuni ʻa ʻeku Tamai kiate au;
And I appoint unto you a kingdom, as my Father hath appointed unto me;
Koeʻuhi ke mou kai mo inu ʻi heʻeku keinangaʻanga ʻi hoku puleʻanga, mo nofo ʻi he ngaahi nofoʻa, ʻo fakamaau ʻae faʻahinga ʻe hongofulu ma ua ʻo ʻIsileli.
That ye may eat and drink at my table in my kingdom, and sit on thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel.
“Pea naʻe pehē ʻe he ʻEiki, Saimone, Saimone, vakai, ʻoku holi ʻa Sētane kiate kimoutolu, koeʻuhi ke ne fakatangaʻi ʻakimoutolu ʻo hangē ko e uite.
And the Lord said, Simon, Simon, behold, Satan hath desired to have you, that he may sift you as wheat:
Ka kuo u hūfia koe, ke ʻoua naʻa mate hoʻo tui: pea ʻoka ke ka toe liliu, ke ke tokoni ho kāinga.”
But I have prayed for thee, that thy faith fail not: and when thou art converted, strengthen thy brethren.
Pea pehē ʻe ia kiate ia, “ʻEiki, te u ʻalu mo koe ki he fale fakapōpula mo e mate.”
And he said unto him, Lord, I am ready to go with thee, both into prison, and to death.
Pea pehē ʻe ia, “Pita, ʻoku ou tala kiate koe, ʻE ʻikai ʻuʻua ʻae moa ʻi he ʻaho ni, kaeʻoua ke tuʻo tolu hao fakafisi, ʻo pehē, ʻoku ʻikai te ke ʻilo au.”
And he said, I tell thee, Peter, the cock shall not crow this day, before that thou shalt thrice deny that thou knowest me.
Pea pehē ʻe ia kiate kinautolu, “ʻI heʻeku fekau atu ʻakimoutolu taʻehakatopaʻanga, pe ha kato kai, pe ha topuvaʻe, naʻa mou masiva ʻi ha meʻa?” Pea nau pehē, “ʻIkai.”
And he said unto them, When I sent you without purse, and scrip, and shoes, lacked ye any thing? And they said, Nothing.

Pea pehē ai ʻe ia kiate kinautolu, “Ka ko eni, ko ia ʻoku maʻu ʻae kato paʻanga, ke ne toʻo ia, pea mo e kato kai foki; pea ko ia ʻoku ʻikai haʻane heletā, ke fakatau ʻe ia ʻa hono kofu, pea maʻu ai ha taha.”
Then said he unto them, But now, he that hath a purse, let him take it, and likewise his scrip: and he that hath no sword, let him sell his garment, and buy one.
He ʻoku ou tala atu kiate kimoutolu, ko e tohi ni, ‘Pea naʻe lau fakataha ia mo e kau angahala,’ ʻe fakamoʻoni ʻiate au: he ko e ngaahi meʻa ʻoku kau kiate au ʻe fakamoʻoni ki ai.”
For I say unto you, that this that is written must yet be accomplished in me, And he was reckoned among the transgressors: for the things concerning me have an end.
Pea naʻa nau pehē, ‘ʻEiki, vakai, ko eni ʻae heletā ʻe ua.” Pea pehē ʻe ia kiate kinautolu, “ʻOku lahi.”
And they said, Lord, behold, here are two swords. And he said unto them, It is enough.
Pea haʻu kituaʻā ia, ʻo ʻalu ki he moʻunga ʻoe ʻOlive, ʻo hangē ko ʻene faʻa fai; pea muimui ʻa ʻene kau ākonga kiate ia.
And he came out, and went, as he was wont, to the mount of Olives; and his disciples also followed him.
Pea kuo hoko ia ki he potu, pea ne pehē kiate kinautolu, “Mou lotu ke ʻoua naʻa mou hinga ki he ʻahiʻahi.”
And when he was at the place, he said unto them, Pray that ye enter not into temptation.
Pea mahuʻi ia ʻiate kinautolu, ʻo hangē ko e lisiʻanga maka hono mamaʻo, pea tūʻulutui, mo lotu,
And he was withdrawn from them about a stone’s cast, and kneeled down, and prayed,
‌ʻo ne pehē, “ʻE Tamai, kapau ko ho finangalo, ʻave ʻae ipu ni ʻiate au: kaeʻoua naʻa fai hoku loto, ka ko e finangalo ʻoʻou.”
Saying, Father, if thou be willing, remove this cup from me: nevertheless not my will, but thine, be done.
Pea naʻe fakahā mai ʻae ʻāngelo mei he langi kiate ia, ʻo ne fakamālohi ia.
And there appeared an angel unto him from heaven, strengthening him.
Pea moʻua ia ʻi he mamahi lahi, pea ʻāsili ai ʻene lotu fakamātoato: pea ko ʻene tautaʻa ko e taʻataʻa naʻe tō ʻi he tulutā lalahi ki he kelekele.
And being in an agony he prayed more earnestly: and his sweat was as it were great drops of blood falling down to the ground.
Pea tuʻu hake ia mei he lotu, ʻo haʻu ia ki heʻene kau ākonga, ʻo ne ʻilo ʻakinautolu ʻoku nau moʻumohea ʻi he mamahi.
And when he rose up from prayer, and was come to his disciples, he found them sleeping for sorrow,
Pea pehē ʻe ia kiate kinautolu, “Ko e hā ʻoku mou mohe ai? Mou tuʻu ʻo lotu, telia naʻa mou tō ki he ʻahiʻahi.”
And said unto them, Why sleep ye? rise and pray, lest ye enter into temptation.
Pea lolotonga ʻene lea, vakai, ko e kakai, pea mo ia naʻe ui ko Siutasi, ko e taha ʻi he toko hongofulu ma toko ua, naʻe muʻomuʻa ia kiate kinautolu, ʻo ne ʻunuʻunu atu kia Sisu ke ʻuma ki ai.
And while he yet spake, behold a multitude, and he that was called Judas, one of the twelve, went before them, and drew near unto Jesus to kiss him.
Ka naʻe pehē ʻe Sisu kiate ia, “Siutasi, ʻoku ke lavakiʻi ʻae Foha ʻoe tangata ʻaki ʻae ʻuma?”
But Jesus said unto him, Judas, betrayest thou the Son of man with a kiss?
Pea kuo mamata ʻakinautolu naʻe ʻiate ia ʻaia ʻe hoko, naʻa nau pehē kiate ia, “ʻEiki, te mau taaʻi ʻaki ʻae heletā?”
When they which were about him saw what would follow, they said unto him, Lord, shall we smite with the sword?
Pea naʻe taaʻi ʻe honau tokotaha ʻae tamaioʻeiki ʻae taulaʻeiki lahi, ʻo ne motuhi hono telinga toʻomataʻu.
And one of them smote the servant of the high priest, and cut off his right ear.
Pea leaange ʻa Sisu, ʻo pehē, “Tukuā, kuo lahi eni.” Pea ne ala ki hono telinga, ʻo fakamoʻui ia.
And Jesus answered and said, Suffer ye thus far. And he touched his ear, and healed him.
Pea pehē ʻe Sisu ki he kau taulaʻeiki lahi, mo e kau pule ʻoe falelotu lahi, mo e kau mātuʻa, naʻe haʻu kiate ia, “Kuo mou omi mo e ngaahi heletā, mo e ngaahi ʻakau, ʻo hangē ki ha kaihaʻa?
Then Jesus said unto the chief priests, and captains of the temple, and the elders, which were come to him, Be ye come out, as against a thief, with swords and staves?
‌ʻI heʻeku ʻiate kimoutolu ʻi he falelotu lahi ʻi he ʻaho kotoa pē, naʻe ʻikai mafao atu ha nima kiate au: ka ko homou feituʻupō eni, mo e mālohi ʻoe fakapoʻuli.”
When I was daily with you in the temple, ye stretched forth no hands against me: but this is your hour, and the power of darkness.
Pea naʻa nau puke ai ia, pea taki ʻo ʻomi ia ki he fale ʻoe taulaʻeiki lahi. Pea naʻe muimui mamaʻo atu ʻa Pita.
Then took they him, and led him, and brought him into the high priest’s house. And Peter followed afar off.
Pea kuo nau tafu ʻae afi ʻi loto fale, ʻonau nonofo fakataha, pea nofo ki lalo ʻa Pita mo kinautolu.
And when they had kindled a fire in the midst of the hall, and were set down together, Peter sat down among them.
Ka naʻe mamata kiate ia ʻae kaunanga ʻe tokotaha ʻi heʻene nofo ofi ki he afi, ʻo ne sio fakamamaʻu kiate ia, mo pehē, “Naʻe ʻiate ia foki ʻae tangata ni.”
But a certain maid beheld him as he sat by the fire, and earnestly looked upon him, and said, This man was also with him.
Pea fakafisi ia, ʻo pehē, “ʻE fefine, ʻoku ʻikai te u ʻilo ia.”
And he denied him, saying, Woman, I know him not.
Pea toe siʻi mo e mamata kiate ia ʻae tokotaha kehe, ʻo ne pehē, “ʻOku ke ʻonautolu foki.” Pea pehēange ʻe Pita, “ʻE tangata, ʻoku ʻikai.”
And after a little while another saw him, and said, Thou art also of them. And Peter said, Man, I am not.
Pea hili nai ʻae feituʻupō ʻe taha, mo ʻene lea fakapapau ʻae tokotaha, ʻo pehē, “Ko e moʻoni naʻe ʻiate ia foki ʻae siana ni; he ko e Kāleli ia.”
And about the space of one hour after another confidently affirmed, saying, Of a truth this fellow also was with him: for he is a Galilaean.
Pea pehēange ʻe Pita, “ʻE tangata, ʻoku ʻikai te u ʻilo ʻaia ʻoku ke lea ki ai.” Pea fakafokifā pe, ʻi heʻene kei lea, naʻe ʻuʻua ʻae moa.
And Peter said, Man, I know not what thou sayest. And immediately, while he yet spake, the cock crew.
Pea tafoki ʻae ʻEiki ki mui, ʻo ne sio kia Pita, pea manatuʻi ʻe Pita ʻae lea ʻae ʻEiki, ʻi heʻene pehē kiate ia, “ʻE teʻeki ai ʻuʻua ʻae moa, kuo tuʻo tolu hao fakafisinga ʻiate au.”
And the Lord turned, and looked upon Peter. And Peter remembered the word of the Lord, how he had said unto him, Before the cock crow, thou shalt deny me thrice.
Pea ʻalu kituʻa ʻa Pita, ʻo tangi mamahi.
And Peter went out, and wept bitterly.
Pea ko e kau tangata naʻe puke ʻa Sisu, naʻa nau manukiʻi ʻo taaʻi ia.
And the men that held Jesus mocked him, and smote him.
Pea hili ʻenau nonoʻo hono mata, naʻa nau sipiʻi hono mata, ʻo fehuʻi kiate ia, ʻo pehē, “Mate mai, Ko hai ia ʻoku ne sipiʻi koe?”
And when they had blindfolded him, they struck him on the face, and asked him, saying, Prophesy, who is it that smote thee?
Pea naʻe lahi ʻae meʻa kovi kehekehe naʻa nau lea ʻaki kiate ia.
And many other things blasphemously spake they against him.
Pea ʻi heʻene ʻaho, naʻe fakataha leva ʻae kau mātuʻa ʻoe kakai mo e kau taulaʻeiki lahi mo e kau tangata tohi, ʻonau taki ia ki honau potu fakamaau, ʻonau pehē,
And as soon as it was day, the elders of the people and the chief priests and the scribes came together, and led him into their council, saying,
“Ko koe ko e Kalaisi? Tala mai kiate kimautolu.” Pea pehē ʻe ia kiate kinautolu, “Kapau te u tala kiate kimoutolu, ʻe ʻikai te mou tui:
Art thou the Christ? tell us. And he said unto them, If I tell you, ye will not believe:
Pea kapau te u fehuʻi foki, ʻe ʻikai te mou tala mai kiate au, pe tukuange au.
And if I also ask you, ye will not answer me, nor let me go.
Ka hili eni, ʻe nofo ʻae Foha ʻoe tangata ʻi he nima toʻomataʻu ʻoe māfimafi ʻoe ʻOtua.”
Hereafter shall the Son of man sit on the right hand of the power of God.
Pea nau pehē ai kotoa pē, “He ko e ʻAlo koe ʻoe ʻOtua?” Pea tala ʻe ia kiate kinautolu, “ʻOku mou pehē, pea ko au ia.”
Then said they all, Art thou then the Son of God? And he said unto them, Ye say that I am.
Pea naʻa nau pehē, “Koeʻumaʻā kiate kitautolu mo ha fakamoʻoni? He kuo tau fanongo ʻakitautolu mei hono fofonga ʻoʻona.”
And they said, What need we any further witness? for we ourselves have heard of his own mouth.
Pea naʻe tutuʻu ʻakinautolu kotoa pē, ʻo taki ia kia Pailato.
And the whole multitude of them arose, and led him unto Pilate.
Pea naʻa nau kamata talatalaakiʻi ia, ʻo pehē, “Naʻa mau ʻilo ʻae siana ni ʻoku ne veuveuki ʻae kakai, ʻo ne taʻofi ʻae tukuhau kia Sisa, ʻo ne pehē, ko ia pe ko e Kalaisi ko e Tuʻi.”
And they began to accuse him, saying, We found this fellow perverting the nation, and forbidding to give tribute to Caesar, saying that he himself is Christ a King.
Pea fehuʻi ʻa Pailato kiate ia, ʻo pehē, “Ko e Tuʻi koe ʻoe kakai Siu?” Pea leaange ʻe ia kiate ia, ʻo pehē, “Ko ia pe.”
And Pilate asked him, saying, Art thou the King of the Jews? And he answered him and said, Thou sayest it.
Pea pehē ai ʻe Pailato ki he kau taulaʻeiki lahi mo e kakai, “ʻOku ʻikai te u ʻilo ha kovi ʻi he tangata ni.”
Then said Pilate to the chief priests and to the people, I find no fault in this man.
Pea ʻāsili ai ʻenau lili, ʻo pehē, “ʻOku ne veuveuki ʻae kakai, ʻo ne ako ʻi Siutea kotoa, ngata mei Kāleli ʻo aʻu ki he potu ni.”
And they were the more fierce, saying, He stirreth up the people, teaching throughout all Jewry, beginning from Galilee to this place.
Pea kuo fanongo ʻa Pailato ki ai, pea fehuʻi ai ia pe ko e tangata Kāleli ia.
When Pilate heard of Galilee, he asked whether the man were a Galilaean.
Pea ʻi heʻene ʻilo ʻoku ne mei he feituʻu ʻoku pule ai ʻa Helota, pea ne fekau ia kia Helota, ʻaia naʻe ʻi Selūsalema foki ʻi he ngaahi ʻaho ko ia.
And as soon as he knew that he belonged unto Herod’s jurisdiction, he sent him to Herod, who himself also was at Jerusalem at that time.

Pea ʻi he mamata ʻa Helota kia Sisu, naʻe fiefia lahi ia; he kuo fuoloa mo ʻene holi ke mamata ki ai, koeʻuhi kuo ne fanongo ki he ngaahi meʻa lahi ʻiate ia: pea ne fakaʻamu ke mamata ki haʻa ne fai ha meʻa mana.
And when Herod saw Jesus, he was exceeding glad: for he was desirous to see him of a long season, because he had heard many things of him; and he hoped to have seen some miracle done by him.
Pea naʻe lahi ʻene ngaahi ʻeke kiate ia, ka naʻe ʻikai siʻi lea ʻe ia ki ai.
Then he questioned with him in many words; but he answered him nothing.
Pea naʻe tutuʻu ʻae kau taulaʻeiki lahi mo e kau tangata tohi, ʻonau talatalaaki mālohi ia.
And the chief priests and scribes stood and vehemently accused him.
Pea taukaea ia ʻe Helota, mo ʻene kautau, mo nau manukiʻi, pea nau ʻai ʻae kofu ngingila kiate ia, ʻo toe fekau ia kia Pailato.
And Herod with his men of war set him at nought, and mocked him, and arrayed him in a gorgeous robe, and sent him again to Pilate.
Pea ko e ʻaho ko ia naʻe feʻofoʻofani ai ʻa Pailato mo Helota: he kuo loa ʻena feʻiteʻitani.
And the same day Pilate and Herod were made friends together: for before they were at enmity between themselves.
Pea kuo fakataha ʻe Pailato ʻae kau taulaʻeiki lahi, mo e kau matāpule, mo e kakai,
And Pilate, when he had called together the chief priests and the rulers and the people,

Pea ne pehē kiate kinautolu, “Kuo mou ʻomi ʻae tangata ni kiate au, ʻo hangē ko ha taha ʻoku ne veuveuki ʻae kakai pea vakai, kuo u ʻekeaia ʻi homou ʻao; pea ʻoku ʻikai te u ʻilo ha kovi ʻoe tangata ni ʻi he ngaahi meʻa ko ia ʻoku mou talatalaakiʻi ai ia:

Said unto them, Ye have brought this man unto me, as one that perverteth the people: and, behold, I, having examined him before you, have found no fault in this man touching those things whereof ye accuse him:
Pea ko Helota foki; he naʻaku fekau ʻakimoutolu kiate ia; pea vakai, ʻoku ʻikai ha meʻa ʻoku totonu ke mate ai ia.”
No, nor yet Herod: for I sent you to him; and, lo, nothing worthy of death is done unto him.
Ko ia te u tautea ia, pea tukuange.”
I will therefore chastise him, and release him.
(He kuo totonu ke ne tukuange kiate kinautolu ha tokotaha ʻi he kātoanga.)
(For of necessity he must release one unto them at the feast.)
Pea naʻa nau kalanga fakataha kotoa pē, ʻo pehē, “ʻAve ʻae tangata ni, kae tuku mai ʻa Palāpasa kiate kimautolu:”
And they cried out all at once, saying, Away with this man, and release unto us Barabbas:
(ʻAia naʻe lī ki he fale fakapōpula, koeʻuhi koʻene fakaaoao ʻi he kolo, mo e fakapō.)
(Who for a certain sedition made in the city, and for murder, was cast into prison.)
Ka naʻe loto ʻa Pailato ke tukuange ʻa Sisu, ko ia ne ne toe lea ai kiate kinautolu.
Pilate therefore, willing to release Jesus, spake again to them.
Ka naʻa nau kalanga, ʻo pehē, “Tutuki ki he ʻakau, tutuki ia ki he ʻakau.”
But they cried, saying, Crucify him, crucify him.
Pea lea ia kiate kinautolu ko hono tuʻo tolu, “Koeʻumaʻā, ko e hā ha kovi kuo ne fai? ʻOku ʻikai te u ʻilo ha meʻa ke mate ai ia: ko ia te u tautea ia, pea tukuange.”
And he said unto them the third time, Why, what evil hath he done? I have found no cause of death in him: I will therefore chastise him, and let him go.
Ka naʻe mālohi ʻenau lea pea longoaʻa lahi, ʻonau pehē, “Ke tutuki ia ki he ʻakau.” Pea naʻe mālohi ʻae leʻo ʻokinautolu mo e kau taulaʻeiki lahi.
And they were instant with loud voices, requiring that he might be crucified. And the voices of them and of the chief priests prevailed.
Pea fekau ʻe Pailato ke fai ʻo hangē ko honau loto.
And Pilate gave sentence that it should be as they required.
Pea ne tukuange kiate kinautolu ia naʻa nau holi ki ai, ʻaia naʻe lī ki he fale fakapōpula, koeʻuhi ko e fakaaoao mo e fakapō; ka ne tukuange ʻa Sisu ki honau loto.
And he released unto them him that for sedition and murder was cast into prison, whom they had desired; but he delivered Jesus to their will.
Pea ʻi heʻenau kei taki atu ia, naʻa nau puke ʻae tokotaha ko Saimone, ko e Sailini, ʻoku haʻu mei he tukuʻuta, pea naʻa nau hili kiate ia ʻae ʻakau, ke ne fua ʻo muimui ia Sisu.
And as they led him away, they laid hold upon one Simon, a Cyrenian, coming out of the country, and on him they laid the cross, that he might bear it after Jesus.
Pea naʻe muimui kiate ia ʻae kakai tokolahi, mo e kau fefine, ʻonau tangi mo tangilāulau koeʻuhi ko ia.
And there followed him a great company of people, and of women, which also bewailed and lamented him.
Ka naʻe tafoki ʻa Sisu kiate kinautolu, ʻo ne pehē, “ʻAe ngaahi ʻofefine ʻo Selūsalema, ʻOua naʻa mou tangi koeʻuhi ko au, kae tangi koeʻuhi ko kimoutolu, pea mo hoʻomou fānau.
But Jesus turning unto them said, Daughters of Jerusalem, weep not for me, but weep for yourselves, and for your children.
Vakai, he ʻoku ofi mai ʻae ngaahi ʻaho te nau pehē ai, ‘ʻOku monūʻia ʻae paʻa, pea mo e manāva naʻe ʻikai fānau, mo e huhū naʻe ʻikai fakahuhūʻaki.’
For, behold, the days are coming, in the which they shall say, Blessed are the barren, and the wombs that never bare, and the paps which never gave suck.
Pea te nau toki kamata lea ai ki he ngaahi moʻunga, “Holo mai kiate kimautolu:” pea ki he ngaahi tafungofunga, “Uʻufi ʻakimautolu.”’
Then shall they begin to say to the mountains, Fall on us; and to the hills, Cover us.
He kapau te nau fai ʻae ngaahi meʻa ni ki he ʻakau mata, ko e hā ʻe fai ki he mōmoa?”
For if they do these things in a green tree, what shall be done in the dry?
Pea naʻe tataki mo ia foki ʻae ongo fai kovi ʻe toko ua ke tāmateʻi.
And there were also two other, malefactors, led with him to be put to death.
Pea kuo nau hoko ki he potu ʻoku ui ko Kalivali, naʻa nau tuki ia ʻi ai ki he ʻakau, mo e ongo fai kovi, ko e tokotaha ki he nima toʻomataʻu, mo e tokotaha ki he nima toʻohema.
And when they were come to the place, which is called Calvary, there they crucified him, and the malefactors, one on the right hand, and the other on the left.
Pea toki pehē ʻe Sisu, “ʻE Tamai, fakamolemole ʻakinautolu; he ʻoku ʻikai te nau ʻilo ʻaia ʻoku nau fai.” Pea naʻa nau vahevahe ʻa hono ngaahi kofu, ʻo talotalo.
Then said Jesus, Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do. And they parted his raiment, and cast lots.
Pea tuʻu ʻae kakai, ʻo mamata. Pea nau manuki mo e kau matāpulekiate ia, ʻo pehē, “Naʻe fakamoʻui ʻe ia ʻae kakai; tuku ke ne fakamoʻui ia, ʻo kapau ko e Kalaisi ia, ko e ʻofeina ʻae ʻOtua.”
And the people stood beholding. And the rulers also with them derided him, saying, He saved others; let him save himself, if he be Christ, the chosen of God.
Pea manukiʻi foki ia ʻe he kau tau, mo nau ʻalu ange, ʻo ʻatu ʻae vaimahi kiate ia,
And the soldiers also mocked him, coming to him, and offering him vinegar,
Mo nau pehē, “Kapau ko e tuʻi koe ʻoe kakai Siu, fakamoʻui koe.”
And saying, If thou be the king of the Jews, save thyself.
Pea naʻe tohi foki ʻi ʻolunga ʻiate ia, ʻae tohi ʻi he lea fakaKiliki, mo e lea fakaLoma, mo e lea fakaHepelū, KO ENI ʻAE TUʻI ʻOE KAKAI SIU.
And a superscription also was written over him in letters of Greek, and Latin, and Hebrew, THIS IS THE KING OF THE JEWS.
Pea naʻe manuki kiate ia ʻae tokotaha ʻoe ongo fai kovi naʻe tautau, ʻo ne pehē, “Kapau ko e Kalaisi koe, fakamoʻui koe mo kimaua.”
And one of the malefactors which were hanged railed on him, saying, If thou be Christ, save thyself and us.
Ka naʻe leaange ʻa hono toko ua, ʻo ne valoki ia, ʻo pehē, “ʻIkai te ke manavahē koe ki he ʻOtua, he ʻoku ke malaʻia foki?
But the other answering rebuked him, saying, Dost not thou fear God, seeing thou art in the same condemnation?
Pea ʻoku totonu kiate kitaua, he ko e totongi totonu ʻo ʻeta ngāue: ka naʻe ʻikai ha kovi ʻe fai ʻe he tangata ni.”
And we indeed justly; for we receive the due reward of our deeds: but this man hath done nothing amiss.
Pea pehē ʻe ia kia Sisu, “ʻEiki ke ke manatuʻi au, ʻoka ke ka hoko ki ho puleʻanga.”
And he said unto Jesus, Lord, remember me when thou comest into thy kingdom.
Pea pehēange ʻe Sisu kiate ia, “ʻOku ou tala moʻoni kiate koe, Te ta ʻi Palataisi mo au he ʻaho ni.”
And Jesus said unto him, Verily I say unto thee, To day shalt thou be with me in paradise.
Pea ko hono ono nai ia ʻoe feituʻulaʻā, pea naʻe fakapoʻuli ʻae fonua kotoa pē, ʻo aʻu ki hono hiva ʻoe feituʻulaʻā.
And it was about the sixth hour, and there was a darkness over all the earth until the ninth hour.
Pea fakapoʻuli ʻae laʻā, pea mahae ua mālie ʻae puipui ʻoe falelotu lahi.
And the sun was darkened, and the veil of the temple was rent in the midst.
Pea tangi leʻo lahi ʻa Sisu, ʻo ne pehē, “ʻE Tamai, ‘ʻoku ou tuku hoku laumālie ki ho nima: pea hili ʻene lea pehē, pea pekia ia.’”
And when Jesus had cried with a loud voice, he said, Father, into thy hands I commend my spirit: and having said thus, he gave up the ghost.
Pea kuo mamata ʻae ʻeikitau ki he meʻa kuo fai, pea fakamālō ia ki he ʻOtua, ʻo ne pehē, “Tā ko e moʻoni ko e tangata māʻoniʻoni eni.”
Now when the centurion saw what was done, he glorified God, saying, Certainly this was a righteous man.
Pea mo e kakai kotoa pē naʻe kātoa ki he vakai ʻoe meʻa ko ia, ʻi heʻenau mamata ki he ngaahi meʻa naʻe fai, naʻa nau si fatafata, ʻo toe ʻalu.
And all the people that came together to that sight, beholding the things which were done, smote their breasts, and returned.
Pea ko hono kāinga kotoa pē, mo e kau fefine naʻe muimui ʻiate ia mei Kāleli, naʻa nau tutuʻu mei he mamaʻo, ʻo vakai ki he ngaahi meʻa ni.
And all his acquaintance, and the women that followed him from Galilee, stood afar off, beholding these things.
Pea vakai, ko e tangata naʻe hingoa ko Siosefa, ko e fakamaau, ko e tangata lelei pea angatonu:
And, behold, there was a man named Joseph, a counsellor; and he was a good man, and a just:
(Naʻe ʻikai loto ia ki he fakakaukau mo e ngāue ʻanautolu:) ko e ʻAlematea ia, ko e kolo ʻoe kakai Siu: pea naʻe tatali foki ia ki he puleʻanga ʻoe ʻOtua.
(The same had not consented to the counsel and deed of them;) he was of Arimathaea, a city of the Jews: who also himself waited for the kingdom of God.
Naʻe ʻalu ia kia Pailato, ʻo ne kole ʻae sino ʻo Sisu.
This man went unto Pilate, and begged the body of Jesus.
Pea ne vete hifo ia, ʻo fakakoloa ʻaki ia ʻae tupenu lelei, ʻo tuku ia ki he fonualoto kuo tā ʻi he loto maka, ʻaia naʻe teʻeki fakatokoto ai ha tokotaha.
And he took it down, and wrapped it in linen, and laid it in a sepulchre that was hewn in stone, wherein never man before was laid.
Pea ko e ʻaho teuteu ia, pea kuo ofi ʻae Sāpate.
And that day was the preparation, and the sabbath drew on.
Ko e kau fefine foki, naʻe omi mo ia mei Kāleli, naʻa nau muimui mai, ʻo, mamata ki he fonualoto, mo e tuku ʻo hono sino.
And the women also, which came with him from Galilee, followed after, and beheld the sepulchre, and how his body was laid.
Pea naʻa nau liu mai, ʻo tokonaki ʻae ngaahi ʻakau namu kakala mo e lolo tākai; pea nau mālōlō ʻi he ʻaho Sāpate ʻo hangē ko e fekau.
And they returned, and prepared spices and ointments; and rested the sabbath day according to the commandment.
Pea ʻi he ʻuluakiʻaho ʻoe uike, ʻi he kei hengihengi, naʻa nau omi mo e niʻihi kehe ki he fonualoto, ʻo ʻomi ʻae ngaahi ʻakau namu kakala kuo nau teuteu.
Now upon the first day of the week, very early in the morning, they came unto the sepulchre, bringing the spices which they had prepared, and certain others with them.
Pea naʻa nau vakai kuo tekaʻi ʻae maka mei he fonualoto.
And they found the stone rolled away from the sepulchre.
Pea naʻa nau hū atu, ka naʻe ʻikai te nau ʻilo ʻae sino ʻoe ʻEiki ko Sisu.
And they entered in, and found not the body of the Lord Jesus.
Pea lolotonga ʻenau puputuʻu lahi ai, vakai, naʻe tuʻu mai kiate kinautolu ʻae ongo tangata naʻe huhulu hona kofu:
And it came to pass, as they were much perplexed thereabout, behold, two men stood by them in shining garments:
Pea ʻi heʻenau manavahē, ʻo tulolo honau mata ki he kelekele, naʻe pehē ʻekinaua kiate kinautolu, “Ko e hā ʻoku mou kumi ai ʻae moʻui ʻi he potu ʻoe mate?
And as they were afraid, and bowed down their faces to the earth, they said unto them, Why seek ye the living among the dead?
‌ʻOku ʻikai ʻi heni ia, ka kuo tuʻu hake: mou fakamanatu ki heʻene lea kiate kimoutolu, ʻi heʻene kei ʻi Kāleli,
He is not here, but is risen: remember how he spake unto you when he was yet in Galilee,
‌ʻo pehē, ‘ʻE tukuange ʻae Foha ʻoe tangata ki he nima ʻoe kau tangata angahala, pea ʻe tutuki ia ki he ʻakau, pea ʻe toetuʻu ia ʻi hono ʻaho tolu.’”
Saying, The Son of man must be delivered into the hands of sinful men, and be crucified, and the third day rise again.
Pea naʻa nau manatu ki heʻene ngaahi lea,
And they remembered his words,
‌ʻO nau liu mai mei he fonualoto, ʻo fakahā ʻae ngaahi meʻa ni kotoa pē ki he toko hongofulu ma tokotaha, mo e kakai kehe kotoa pē.
And returned from the sepulchre, and told all these things unto the eleven, and to all the rest.
Pea ko Mele Makitaline, mo Soana, mo Mele ko e faʻē ʻa Semisi, pea mo e niʻihi naʻe ʻiate kinautolu, naʻa nau fakahā ʻae ngaahi meʻa ni ki he kau ʻaposetolo.
It was Mary Magdalene, and Joanna, and Mary the mother of James, and other women that were with them, which told these things unto the apostles.
Pea naʻe tatau ʻenau ngaahi lea kiate kinautolu mo e talanoa launoa, pea naʻe ʻikai te nau tui kiate kinautolu.
And their words seemed to them as idle tales, and they believed them not.
Pea toki tuʻu ʻa Pita, ʻo lele ki he fonualoto; pea tulolo ia, ʻo mamata ki he u kofu kuo tuku kehe, pea ʻalu ia, ʻo fakatumutumu ʻi hono loto ʻi he meʻa kuo hoko.
Then arose Peter, and ran unto the sepulchre; and stooping down, he beheld the linen clothes laid by themselves, and departed, wondering in himself at that which was come to pass.
Pea vakai, naʻe ʻo ʻa honau toko ua, ʻi he ʻaho ko ia, ki he potu kakai naʻe ui ko ʻEmeasi, naʻe mamaʻo mo Selūsalema, ko e maile ʻe fitu.
And, behold, two of them went that same day to a village called Emmaus, which was from Jerusalem about threescore furlongs.
Pea naʻa na talanoa ki he ngaahi meʻa ni kotoa pē kuo toki hoko,
And they talked together of all these things which had happened.
Pea lolotonga ʻae fai ʻena talanoa mo ʻena fakakaukau, mo ʻene ʻunuʻunu atu ʻa Sisu, ʻo fononga mo kinaua.
And it came to pass, that, while they communed together and reasoned, Jesus himself drew near, and went with them.
Ka naʻe taʻofi ʻa hona mata, ke ʻoua naʻa na ʻilo ia.
But their eyes were holden that they should not know him.
Pea pehē ʻe ia kiate kinaua, “Ko e talanoa hā ia ʻoku mo fetalanoaʻaki ʻi hoʻomo fononga, pea mo mamahi ai?”
And he said unto them, What manner of communications are these that ye have one to another, as ye walk, and are sad?
Pea ko e tokotaha, ko Kaliopasi hono hingoa, naʻe lea ʻo pehē kiate ia, naʻa ko Koe pe ʻoku nofo ʻi Selūsalema pea ʻoku ʻikai te ke ʻilo ʻae ngaahi meʻa kuo hoko ʻi ai ʻi he ngaahi ʻaho ni?
And the one of them, whose name was Cleopas, answering said unto him, Art thou only a stranger in Jerusalem, and hast not known the things which are come to pass there in these days?
Pea pehē ʻe ia kiate kinaua, “Ko e hā ʻae meʻa?” Pea na pehē kiate ia, “Kia Sisu ʻo Nāsaleti, ko e palōfita naʻe mālohi ʻi he ngāue mo e lea ʻi he ʻao ʻoe ʻOtua mo e kakai kotoa pē:
And he said unto them, What things? And they said unto him, Concerning Jesus of Nazareth, which was a prophet mighty in deed and word before God and all the people:
Pea mo e tukuange ia ʻe homau kau taulaʻeiki lahi mo e kau fakamaau ke tāmateʻi, pea kuo tutuki ia ki he ʻakau.
And how the chief priests and our rulers delivered him to be condemned to death, and have crucified him.
Ka naʻa mau falala ko ia ia te ne huhuʻi ʻa ʻIsileli: kaeʻumaʻā eni kotoa pē, ko hono ʻaho tolu eni talu hono fai ʻae ngaahi meʻa ni.
But we trusted that it had been he which should have redeemed Israel: and beside all this, to day is the third day since these things were done.
‌ʻIo, pea fakaofo kiate kimautolu ʻe homau kau fefine niʻihi, naʻa nau ʻalu hengihengi ki he fonualoto;
Yea, and certain women also of our company made us astonished, which were early at the sepulchre;
Pea ʻi he ʻikai te nau ʻilo hono sino, naʻa nau haʻu, ʻo pehē, kuo nau mamata foki ki he kau ʻāngelo, pea nau pehē, kuo moʻui ia.
And when they found not his body, they came, saying, that they had also seen a vision of angels, which said that he was alive.
Pea ko homau niʻihi naʻe ʻalu ki he fonualoto, ʻonau ʻilo ʻo hangē pe ko ia naʻe fakahā ʻe he kau fefine: ka naʻe ʻikai te nau mamata kiate ia.”
And certain of them which were with us went to the sepulchre, and found it even so as the women had said: but him they saw not.
Pea toki pehē ʻe ia kiate kinaua, “ʻAe kau vale, mo loto tuai ke tui ki he meʻa kotoa pē naʻe lea ʻaki ʻe he kau palōfita:
Then he said unto them, O fools, and slow of heart to believe all that the prophets have spoken:
He ʻikai naʻe totonu kia Kalaisi ke kātaki ʻae ngaahi meʻa ni, pea hū ai ki hono nāunau?”
Ought not Christ to have suffered these things, and to enter into his glory?
Pea kamata ia meia Mōsese, ʻo hoko ki he kau palōfita kotoa pē, ʻa ʻene fakamatala kiate kinaua mei he tohi ʻae ngaahi meʻa kotoa pē ʻoku kau kiate ia.
And beginning at Moses and all the prophets, he expounded unto them in all the scriptures the things concerning himself.
Pea kuo nau ofi ki he potu kakai naʻa nau ō ki ai; pea naʻe fai ʻe ia ʻo hangē naʻe fie ʻalu atu pe.
And they drew nigh unto the village, whither they went: and he made as though he would have gone further.
Ka naʻa na taʻofi ia, ʻo pehē, “Ke tau nonofo; he kuo ofi ʻae poʻuli, pea kuo tei ʻosi ʻae ʻaho.” Pea naʻe hū ia ki loto, ke nau nonofo.
But they constrained him, saying, Abide with us: for it is toward evening, and the day is far spent. And he went in to tarry with them.
Pea naʻe hoko ʻo pehē, ʻi heʻenau nofo mo ia ʻi he kai, naʻe toʻo ʻe ia ʻae mā, ʻo ne tāpuaki, pea ne tofi ʻo ʻatu kiate kinaua.
And it came to pass, as he sat at meat with them, he took bread, and blessed it, and brake, and gave to them.
Pea ʻā ai hona mata, ʻo na ʻilo ia pea ʻiloange, kuo mole ia ʻi hona ʻao.
And their eyes were opened, and they knew him; and he vanished out of their sight.
Pea naʻa na fepehēʻaki, “ʻIkai naʻe vela hota loto ʻiate kitaua, ʻi heʻene talanoa mai ʻi he hala kiate kitaua, mo ʻene fakahā ʻae tohi kiate kitaua?”
And they said one to another, Did not our heart burn within us, while he talked with us by the way, and while he opened to us the scriptures?
Pea na tuʻu hake ʻi he feituʻu ʻaho ko ia, ʻo liu mai ki Selūsalema, ʻo na ʻilo ʻae toko hongofulu ma tokotaha kuo kātoa, mo kinautolu naʻe ʻiate kinautolu,
And they rose up the same hour, and returned to Jerusalem, and found the eleven gathered together, and them that were with them,
‌ʻonau pehē, “Kuo toetuʻu moʻoni ʻae ʻEiki, pea kuo fakahā ia kia Saimone.”
Saying, The Lord is risen indeed, and hath appeared to Simon.
Pea tala ʻekinaua ʻae ngaahi meʻa naʻe fai ʻi he hala, pea mo ʻena ʻilo ia ʻi he tofi ʻoe mā.
And they told what things were done in the way, and how he was known of them in breaking of bread.
Pea lolotonga ʻenau lea pehē, mo e tuʻu ʻa Sisu ʻi honau haʻohaʻonga, ʻo ne pehē kiate kinautolu, “Fiemālie pe ʻakimoutolu.”
And as they thus spake, Jesus himself stood in the midst of them, and saith unto them, Peace be unto you.
Pea naʻa nau tāfuʻua mo ilifia, ʻo mahalo kuo nau mamata ki ha laumālie.
But they were terrified and affrighted, and supposed that they had seen a spirit.
Pea pehē ʻe ia kiate kinautolu, “Ko e hā ʻoku mou ilifia ai? Pea ko e hā ʻoku tupu ai ʻae ngaahi mahalo ʻi homou loto?
And he said unto them, Why are ye troubled? and why do thoughts arise in your hearts?
Vakai ki hoku nima mo hoku vaʻe, ko au pe ia: ala mai kiate au, pea mou vakai; he ʻoku ʻikai kakano mo hui ha laumālie, ʻo hangē ko ia ʻoku mou ʻilo ni ʻiate au.”
Behold my hands and my feet, that it is I myself: handle me, and see; for a spirit hath not flesh and bones, as ye see me have.
Pea hili ʻene lea ko ia, naʻa ne toki fakahā kiate kinautolu ʻa hono nima mo hono vaʻe.
And when he had thus spoken, he shewed them his hands and his feet.
Pea ʻi he teʻeki ai te nau tui, ko e meʻa ʻi he fiefia, ka nau ofo pe, pea pehē ʻe ia kiate kinautolu, “ʻOku ʻi heni ha meʻakai?”
And while they yet believed not for joy, and wondered, he said unto them, Have ye here any meat?
Pea nau ange kiate ia ʻae konga ika kuo tunu, mo e ngeʻesi hone.
And they gave him a piece of a broiled fish, and of an honeycomb.
Pea ne toʻo ia, ʻo kai ʻi honau ʻao.
And he took it, and did eat before them.

Pea pehē ʻe ia kiate kinautolu, “Ko eni ʻae ngaahi lea naʻaku lea ʻaki kiate kimoutolu ʻi heʻeku kei ʻiate kimoutolu, koeʻuhi ke fakamoʻoni ʻae ngaahi meʻa kotoa pē, ʻaia kuo tohi kiate au, ʻi he fono ʻa Mōsese, mo e kau palōfita, mo e ngaahi Saame.”

And he said unto them, These are the words which I spake unto you, while I was yet with you, that all things must be fulfilled, which were written in the law of Moses, and in the prophets, and in the psalms, concerning me.
Pea toki toʻo ʻe ia ʻa honau loto, koeʻuhi ke nau ʻilo ʻae ngaahi tohi,
Then opened he their understanding, that they might understand the scriptures,
‌ʻo ne pehē kiate kinautolu, “Kuo pehē ʻae tohi, pea ʻoku taau mo Kalaisi ke mamahi pehē, pea toetuʻu mei he mate ʻi hono ʻaho tolu:
And said unto them, Thus it is written, and thus it behoved Christ to suffer, and to rise from the dead the third day:
Pea ke malangaʻaki ʻae fakatomala, mo e fakamolemole ʻoe angahala ʻi hono hingoa, ʻi he puleʻanga kotoa pē, ʻo fuofua fai ʻi Selūsalema.
And that repentance and remission of sins should be preached in his name among all nations, beginning at Jerusalem.
Pea ko e kau fakamoʻoni ʻakimoutolu ʻoe ngaahi meʻa ni.
And ye are witnesses of these things.
Pea vakai, te u fekau kiate kimoutolu ʻae talaʻofa ʻa ʻeku Tamai: ka mou tatali ʻi he kolo ko Selūsalema, kaeʻoua ke mou maʻu ʻae mālohi mei ʻolunga.”
And, behold, I send the promise of my Father upon you: but tarry ye in the city of Jerusalem, until ye be endued with power from on high.
Pea ne tataki atu ʻakinautolu ʻo aʻu ki Pētani, pea naʻa ne hiki hake hono nima, ʻo tāpuaki ʻakinautolu.
And he led them out as far as to Bethany, and he lifted up his hands, and blessed them.
Pea ʻiloange ʻi he lolotonga ʻene tāpuaki ʻakinautolu, naʻe mavahe ia meiate kinautolu, pea fua hake ia ki he langi.
And it came to pass, while he blessed them, he was parted from them, and carried up into heaven.
Pea naʻa nau hū kiate ia, pea liu mai ki Selūsalema ʻi he fiefia lahi:
And they worshipped him, and returned to Jerusalem with great joy:
Mo nau nofomaʻu ʻi he falelotu lahi, ʻo fakamālō mo fakafetaʻi ki he ʻOtua. ʻEmeni.
And were continually in the temple, praising and blessing God. Amen.
